descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify key details in a text.
I can indicate two or more key details given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, and print).
I can when given an excerpt about George Washington from an informational text, identify the name George and his picture.
I can when given a brochure about the apple orchard, identify an apple tree.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify details in familiar text.
I can identify key details related to a text given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, print).
I can when presented with options, indicate whether a detail is in a familiar text (e.g., daily schedules, lunch menus, calendars).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with prompting, identify a detail in text.
I can identify a detail related to a text given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, and print).
I can when asked, “Did you see/hear this?” indicate whether a detail is present.
I can remember and identify key detail that the teacher just mentioned in a the picture.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with prompts and support, orient to materials related to a text or books.
I can explore text that gives information (e.g., daily schedules, lunch menus, calendars).

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.1|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.2|1.text: Identify a main topic or central idea in a text with guidance and support; retell important details. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.2|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, identify important details(RI) and recount major events (RL) in familiar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify the main idea of a text and explain how the key details support the main idea in my own words.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify the main topic or central idea in a text and retell important details with support.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some details in a text with help and attempt to retell them.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can find the main topic or idea of a text when someone helps me.
I can tell one important detail from a story or text with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the most important details from a story or text I have read or heard.
I can retell the main events of a story in order after reading or listening.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize a few important details from a story or text with help.
I can tell one or two events from a familiar story after reading or listening with some support.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say a detail from a story or text with guidance.
I can use pictures or gestures to show something I remember from a familiar story.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.2|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.3|1.text: Describe characters, settings, and important events in a story or pieces of information in a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.3|1.ee_text: Identify characters and settings (RL) or important details and events (RI) in familiar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can describe characters, settings, and events in a story with lots of detail and explain how they connect to the story's overall meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe characters, settings, and important events in a story or text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe characters or settings in a story with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify the characters and settings in a familiar text.
I can indicate characters and settings given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, print).
I can during a shared reading interaction, point to illustrations that reflect the characters or settings in a story.
I can pick out the character and setting of a familiar story when given choices (e.g., Clifford lives on Birdwell Island with Emily Elizabeth).
I can, after listening to Horton Hears a Who, when given three pictures, pick the elephant as the main character.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify characters and settings in a familiar text.
I can indicate characters and settings from a familiar story given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, and print).
I can during a shared reading interaction with a familiar story, point to illustrations that reflect the characters or settings in a story.
I can given two pictures (one of a character and one of the setting), identify which is the character and which is the setting in a familiar story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify a character or the setting in a familiar text.
I can with guidance and support, indicate characters and settings from a familiar story given a field of choices (e.g., pictures, objects, symbols, and print).
I can during a shared reading interaction with a familiar story and guidance and support from the reader, point to illustrations that reflect the characters or setting in a story.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support and a story that includes people in the student’s life, identify the person in the text.
I can given a story about a class trip that includes photos of classmates and the names of classmates in the text, as well as guidance and support, the student will identify from a field of choices which classmate is featured on a given page.
I can given a story about a personal experience, as well as guidance and support, identify himself/herself as the person who is in the story (e.g., Teacher reads a page and shows the picture and asks, “Who is this book about? Who is that?” and the child responds “me” by patting own chest.).

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.3|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.4|1.text: Identify specific words and phrases that express feeling, appeal to the senses, or content-specific words within a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.4|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, identify sensory or feeling words in a familiar text; ask the reader to explain the meaning of unknown words. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find words in a text that express feelings or appeal to the senses and explain why the author used them.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify words and phrases that show feelings or describe things I can see, hear, touch, taste, or smell.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find simple words in a story that show feelings or describe something I can sense with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify sensory or feeling words in a story.
I can while listening to a story, signal when a feeling word is read.
I can given a picture book that includes illustrations that depict different feelings (e.g., Today, I Feel Silly and Other Moods That Make My Day), identify the feelings as they are depicted on several pages.
I can match a sensory or feeling word to the correct illustration from a story.
I can after hearing a story for the first time, tells the teacher how the main character was feeling: sad, happy, mad, hungry, tired, etc.
I can after reading The Very Hungry Caterpillar, pick hungry from three options when asked, “How was the caterpillar feeling?”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify sensory or feeling words in a familiar story.
I can while listening to a familiar story, signal when a feeling word is read.
I can given a familiar picture book that includes illustrations that depict a feeling (e.g., Today, I Feel Silly and Other Moods That Make My Day), identify the feeling depicted.
I can choose from an array of pictures to identify a sensory or feeling word from a familiar story.
I can Teacher hands a happy card and a sad card to the student and says, “When we are reading the story, hold up the card when you hear ‘happy’ or ‘sad’.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify a specified sensory or feeling word in a familiar story.
I can with guidance and support, as well as a familiar story, use a single message voice output device to say a feeling word after it is read in a text in order to signal recognition of the word.
I can with guidance and support, as well as a familiar story, use a single message voice output device to say a sensory word that the adult reads (e.g., Teacher might say, “The animals in this book use their eyes to see. You help me read by saying the word see with me.” Then, use an exaggerated pause before reading see.).
I can choose from two pictures to identify a sensory or feeling word from the story.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, imitate, act out, or otherwise gesture to demonstrate a sensory or feeling word that is used in a familiar text.
I can with guidance and support, imitate facial expressions to match the feelings in the text, Today, I Feel Silly and Other Moods That Make My Day.
I can with guidance and support, wave a finger to match the words Mrs. Wishy Washy says when she tells each animal, “In the tub you go!”

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.4|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.5|1.text: Identify a variety of genres and explain major differences between literary texts and informational texts. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.5|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, identify a text as telling a story or teaching facts (i.e., informational) and locate the front cover, back cover, and title page of the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can identify different types of books like stories, poems, and informational texts, and explain how they are used for different purposes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify different types of texts like stories and informational books, and explain how they are different.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a book is a story or gives information with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can tell if a book is a story or teaches something with support.
I can say one difference between a story and an information book when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell if a book is a story or gives information.
I can find the front cover, back cover, and title page of a book.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can tell if a book is for fun or for learning with help.
I can point to the front or back cover of a book when asked.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize a book cover with guidance.
I can point to parts of a book, like the front or back, with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.5|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.6|1.text: Describe how illustrations and details support the point of view or purpose of the text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.6|1.ee_text: Distinguish between words and illustrations/graphics in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how pictures and details in a story or informational text help show the author’s point of view and purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how pictures and details help explain the purpose of a text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can point to pictures and details that explain something in the text with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can look at pictures in a book and say what they are showing with help.
I can tell how a picture helps me understand the story or information with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can point to the words in a book and explain how they are different from pictures.
I can say or point to where the pictures and words are in a book.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can point to a word and a picture in a book when asked.
I can find words or pictures in a familiar text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture when reading a book with help.
I can recognize a word in a book with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.6|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.7|1.text: Use illustrations and details in literary and informational texts to discuss story elements or topics. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.7|1.ee_text: Identify illustrations or objects/tactile information that go with the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use pictures and details in a story or informational text to explain the topic or main ideas in my own words.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use pictures and details to talk about the story or topic in a book.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use pictures in a book to talk about what is happening with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use pictures to talk about the characters or events in a story with support.
I can talk about the details in a picture to explain an idea in an informational text when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can find a picture that matches what the text says.
I can point to objects or images that show what the book is about.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find a picture in the book that matches part of the story with some help.
I can point to something in a picture that matches the story when asked.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can look at a picture in a book while someone reads to me.
I can find an object or picture that goes with a story with support.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.7|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.8|1.text: Identify specific information an author or illustrator gives that supports ideas in a text. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.8|1.ee_text: Identify points the author makes in familiar text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how the author’s words and the illustrator’s pictures give information that supports ideas in the text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can find information the author or illustrator gives that helps support ideas in a text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find details in a text that give information about the main idea with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can find a piece of information the author gives in a text with help.
I can talk about how a picture or words help me understand an idea with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell one or two important points the author makes in a story or text.
I can explain what the author wants me to learn from the text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or point to something important the author says in a text.
I can recognize one point the author makes with some help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond when asked about an important point in a familiar text.
I can point to or name something from the text that the author says with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.8|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.9|1.text: Compare and contrast two texts; recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.1.9|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, compare parts of two texts, identifying adventures or experiences of characters in a text as same or different. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare two stories or informational texts, explaining how they are the same or different, and recognize how they show different cultures or ideas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare two texts and talk about how they are alike or different.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find things that are the same or different in two books with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can talk about how two books are the same or different with help.
I can recognize a story that is similar to my life or someone else’s, with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell how characters' adventures or experiences are the same or different in two stories.
I can compare parts of two stories to see what is the same or different.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say how one character in a story is the same or different from another character.
I can tell one thing that is the same or different in two stories with some help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say one thing that is different or the same in two stories with help.
I can use pictures to show how something is the same or different in two stories.

WI-CC-ELA|R.1.9|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.1|1.text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.1|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low- stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write different types of texts, including stories, letters, and reflections, using creativity and proper form, and explain why I chose a particular type of writing for different situations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write creative and formal pieces for different purposes like stories, letters, or personal reflections.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write simple sentences or short pieces about my thoughts or experiences with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can select a selected topic or book and use drawing, dictating, or writing to state an opinion about it.
I can select a book from a collection offered by the teacher and express an opinion about it by writing.
I can given the directions to write about a favorite book, select a book from the classroom library and type letters on an alternate keyboard to write about it.
I can during independent writing, select a familiar book from a selection of three offered by the teacher and write letters to express an opinion about it.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a book and use drawing, dictating, or writing to state an opinion about it.
I can Select a book from a collection offered by the teacher and express an opinion about it by drawing a picture of a happy face.
I can In structured shared writing during which the teacher uses a repeated sentence frame to guide students in creating a predictable chart with the repeated line, I like <type of animal> because they are <descriptor>, the student will select a picture of their favorite animal to communicate which animal they like and then select from an array of possible adjectives reasons why (e.g., “I like <panthers> because they are <strong>.”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a book and use drawing, dictating, or writing to state an opinion about it.
I can select a favorite book to name to be used in a shared writing activity (e.g., During structured shared writing aimed at reviewing favorite books, the teacher provides the repeated line, I like . . ., and students select a favorite book and dictates the name for the teacher to use in completing the sentence.).
I can given the directions to write about a favorite book, select a book from the classroom library, and dictate “I like it” for the teacher to write.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate a preference for a book.
I can select a book from a choice of two by looking at or reaching for it, and, given access to a like/dislike symbol, indicate opinion, which the teacher will write and read aloud (e.g., “Jennifer likes this book.”).
I can select a book from a basket of books, look at it, and, given access to a feelings page of emotion symbols, indicate an opinion about the book that the teacher will write.
I can select an electronic book from a field of two or more books, look at and listen to it, and, given access to appropriate symbols, indicate opinion, which teacher will write and read aloud (e.g., “I don’t like this book.”).

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.1|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.a|1.text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or name the text they are writing about, state an opinion, supply a reason for the opinion, and provide some sense of closure.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.a|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an opinion piece where I introduce the topic, clearly state my opinion, provide several reasons to support my opinion, and finish with a strong conclusion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an opinion piece by introducing the topic, stating my opinion, giving a reason, and finishing with a conclusion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write about my opinion and give a reason with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can name a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about it.
I can use a multiple message voice output device to communicate a topic of choice of writing (e.g., friends) and then uses the device to select words that provide information about friends.
I can Tell the teacher a topic for writing and then dictate information about it.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about it.
I can select a topic from an array of choices and uses drawing, dictating, writing, assistive technology, or other means of expression to convey a feeling, thought, idea, or need relative to the topic.
I can select “my birthday” as a topic and draws a picture of something he or she wants.
I can after choosing to write about him/herself, use drawing, dictating, writing, assistive technology, or other means of expression to state a fact about themselves.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about a topic.
I can after discussing favorite things with a small group, use drawing and writing to communicate about own favorite things.
I can in structured shared writing entitled “Animals,” during which the teacher uses a repeated sentence frame to guide students in creating a predictable chart with the repeated line, The <animal> is <color>, select an appropriate animal which the teacher will write on the chart (e.g., The panther is black. The dog is brown.).
I can given a structured sentence, choose a classmate, and select from a couple of descriptor symbols to complete the statement: <Name> is <descriptor> (e.g., Dallas is short. Erin is happy.), which are added to a class chart text.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic.
I can after the teacher presents two of the student’s favorite toys, select one when asked, “What should we write about today?”
I can work with a group of peers on a writing topic (e.g., The peers narrow down the choices and then presents two to the student who says, “What should we write about today?”).
I can given a selection of topics and with partner-assisted scanning, choose a topic of interest.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.a|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.b|1.text: Informative or explanatory text in which they name a topic, supply some facts about the topic, and provide some sense of closure.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.b|1.ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they provide some information about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an informative text about a topic, give facts with clear explanations, and wrap up my writing with a conclusion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an informative text by naming a topic, giving facts about it, and ending with a conclusion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write facts about a topic with some help, and try to finish with an ending.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about a topic and give one fact with help.
I can finish my writing by adding a sentence when someone guides me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or say facts about a topic I know.
I can give some information about a topic with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write or say one fact about a topic with some help.
I can give a simple piece of information about a topic with support.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say a word or picture about a topic I know with guidance.
I can give information using pictures or words with help.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.b|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.c|1.text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narratives in which they recount two or more appropriately sequenced events, include some details regarding what happened, use temporal words to signal event order, and provide some sense of closure
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.c|1.ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a narrative about real or imagined events, use time-order words to describe what happened, and end my story in an interesting way.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write a story with two or more events in the right order, add details about what happened, and end the story.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write about events in a story and use words like "first" and "next" with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about one or two things that happened with help.
I can tell what happened next in my story when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or talk about something that happened in order.
I can tell a story about something real or made up with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or write one event from a story or my own experience.
I can tell one thing that happened in a story or event with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture or say a word about something that happened with guidance.
I can use words or pictures to show one part of a story or event.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.2.c|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.a|1.text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Provide a beginning, middle and a simple ending
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.a|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses words familiar to the student.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a story or a piece of writing with a clear beginning, middle, and ending, using details to make my story interesting and flow smoothly.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can organize my writing by including a beginning, middle, and ending.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a simple beginning and try to add a middle and ending with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can introduce or name events and use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about them.
I can during a field trip, tell the teacher three things that happened, and upon returning to the classroom, draw and/or write about those things in a three-panel frame in the order they occurred.
I can follow a historical text teacher read-aloud, recount events remembered in a small group, individually choose two events from those recalled, and draw/write about them beginning each recount with “first,” and then “second.”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select an event and use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about it.
I can during a shared writing activity, draw a picture of a class field trip to a zoo that describes an event (a bus ride) from the trip.
I can use a multiple message voice output device to dictate information about an experience during a learning center (e.g., big, bubble, pop, blow, more).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select an event and use drawing, dictating, or writing to share information about it.
I can given an array of photos from a class activity, select one of the pictures, spend time talking about the event depicted in the picture with an adult or peer, and then label it verbally while the teacher writes the labels.
I can work with a teacher who is modeling how to select messages on a multiple message voice output device, select messages to dictate information about an experience during a learning center (e.g., read, funny, book, friends, fun).
I can work with the teacher before snack (or other daily activities), brainstorm the actions of familiar routines, then select one for the teacher to write on a chart (e.g., wash hands, eat snack, eat lunch).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a preferred event or activity.
I can point to or use partner-assisted scanning to choose a preferred event or activity from a picture menu of items, 
I can given a choice of activities for free time represented with pictures or objects, select a preferred activity by looking, touching, or pointing, which the teacher places on personal schedule, writing it and reading aloud.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.a|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.b|1.text: Transitions: Use simple word transitions and temporal words or pictures that link ideas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use time words like "first," "then," and "finally" to link the events in my writing and make it easy to follow.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use simple transition words to show the order of events in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use words like "and then" to connect ideas in my writing with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use words like "first" and "then" to talk about what happens in my story with help.
I can use pictures to show what happens in my story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.b|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.c|1.text: Word Choice (including domain specific): Experiment with descriptive words to describe feelings, events, and images.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose descriptive words to make my writing more interesting and help readers understand my feelings, events, and images.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use descriptive words to describe how things look, feel, or happen in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use simple words to describe things and try new words with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use simple words to describe how I feel or what I see with help.
I can try out new words to describe things in my story when someone supports me.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.3.c|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.4|1.text: With guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task and purpose. (Grade- specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can independently write about topics that show respect for my culture and others, while organizing my writing clearly for the task.
I can develop my writing in a way that is authentic to my voice and the purpose of the assignment, with little to no support.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write about my culture or experiences and organize my writing to match the task and purpose, with some guidance.
I can use appropriate details and organize my writing to stay focused on the topic or purpose of my work.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write about something important to me, and with help, make sure it fits the task and purpose.
I can organize my writing with guidance so that it makes sense for the assignment.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about my ideas or culture with help, and organize my writing with support from an adult.
I can get help to make my writing match the task or purpose, while sharing something about my experiences.
descriptors.ee_at_target: (Begins in grade 3).

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.4|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.5|1.text: With guidance and support from adults, focus on a topic, respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and add details to strengthen writing as needed.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.5|1.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, add more information to their own drawing, dictation, or writing on a topic to strengthen it.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can focus on a topic, listen to feedback from peers and teachers, and add interesting details to make my writing stronger and more detailed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can stay on topic in my writing, listen to suggestions, and add details when needed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write about a topic and make changes with help from my teacher or friends.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing to strengthen it.
I can after sharing own writing with peers, add more detail to the picture to make it better.
I can after looking at writing from a previous day, select to add more to it rather than starting a new piece.
I can react to peer’s responses regarding a writing project (e.g., smile, vocalization, gesture, eye contact) and make a revision of my project.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing to strengthen it.
I can after sharing own writing about a topic with the teacher, add more writing when the teacher asks, “Can you tell me more? What else can you write?”
I can after dictating a story about a self-selected topic to a teacher, say more when the teacher asks, “What else can you tell me about that?”
I can after sharing a drawn, dictated, or written text, add more when the teacher asks, “What else can you add?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, draw, dictate, or write more when asked.
I can during writing time, keep drawing when the teacher says, “Keep going. What else can you tell us?”
I can while writing on a computer listening to the speech feedback from a talking word processor, continue to add more letters when the teacher says, “Tell us more. You know so much about <whatever initiated the writing>.”
I can take turns typing letters or words about a picture or shared experience with a proficient or advanced peer using an adapted keyboard with only letters and a spacebar available.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, explore tools for drawing, writing, and self-expression.
I can touch, bang on, or otherwise interact with a computer keyboard when presented with a photo of a favorite activity, person, or place, and when directed by the teacher to “Tell me more,” touch, bang on, or otherwise interact with the keyboard some more.
I can make marks on a paper with a crayon when it is presented.
I can after a teacher models a simple message on a student’s first draft and provides invitation, student explores writing further (e.g., “Run. I see that dog in the picture run.”).

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.5|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.6|1.text: With guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming most printed upper- and lower-case letters), cursive, or typing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.6|1.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, explore a variety of digital tools to produce individual or group writing. With guidance and support from adults, produce writing through printing (including letter- like marks or forming some printed letters).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use digital tools like computers or tablets to publish my writing and work with classmates to create shared projects, while also practicing both printing and typing letters.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use digital tools like computers or tablets to create and publish my writing with help, and I can print most upper- and lower-case letters correctly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a computer or tablet with help to write and try forming some printed letters.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use a variety of digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can work with peers at an interactive whiteboard, select from an array of pictures and type some letters using the onscreen keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
I can work with peers, select words and pictures from an alternative keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher while working with peers at an interactive whiteboard, select from an array of pictures and types some letters using the onscreen keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher while working with peers, selects words and pictures from an alternative keyboard to add to the group’s writing.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, explore digital tools to produce writing, including in collaboration with peers.
I can explore teacher-selected form of technology appropriate to the individual student to produce a product for the teacher to print and post on the bulletin board.
I can explore technology that supports writing and communication with peers (e.g., use a switch or touchscreen to communicate meaningfully).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, explore various means of accessing digital tools.
I can activate a switch to scan through the letters of the alphabet.
I can touch, bang, or swipe over the surface of an alternative keyboard to produce a product for the teacher to print and post on the bulletin board.
I can touch a touchscreen on a computer or tablet device for a peer to print to include in a class book entitled, This Week’s Writing.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.6|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.7|1.text: Participate in shared inquiry and writing projects (e.g., explore a number of “how-to” books on a given topic and use them to write a sequence of instructions).
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.7|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in shared inquiry and writing projects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can work with others to explore different books and write detailed instructions or a project plan using what we’ve learned.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can work with others to explore “how-to” books and write a sequence of instructions for a project or activity.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can work with others and write simple steps for a project or activity with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can participate to share research and writing projects with others.
I can identify pictures and words to include in a shared research project on a familiar topic (e.g., “what we know about whales,” point to relevant pictures and words from a book about whales).
I can select the topic of the research project and choose words or ideas to include.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can participate in shared research and writing projects.
I can select a book on a topic related to a shared research project from a collection identified by peers and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched.
I can type letters as they are dictated by a peer to add content to a shared writing project.
I can Recall information from a shared school experience and participate in a shared writing project to list details from that experience.
I can listen to an electronic book appropriate to the research and writing project, and share one fact with the group to include in the project.
I can listen with a peer to electronic books selected by the teacher in a digital reading environment and with a keyboard with alphabet and whole word access, type letters, words, or sentences about what they learn.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, participate in shared research and writing projects.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher, select a book from a choice of two related to the shared research project and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched.
I can given a premade set-up on an alternative keyboard or onscreen keyboard, select words and pictures to add to a shared research and writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with prompts and support, explore pictures, words, or objects related to a shared research project.
I can given a multimedia presentation of words and pictures related to a shared research project, use a switch to advance through the pictures looking and/or listening to the words and pictures.
I can use a touchscreen to scroll through pictures related to the topic of a shared research project.
I can explore a bin full of objects and artifacts related to a shared research project.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.7|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.8|1.text: With guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.8|1.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can gather information from different sources or my own experiences to answer questions and explain my answers in detail.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can remember or find information to answer a question with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can remember or find some information to answer a question with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults, recall information from experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, recall information from a recent school book fair for the teacher to write down (e.g., “book,” “money,” “library”) and then answer the teacher’s question when she asks, “Do you like the book?”
I can work with a small group and the teacher, recall information from a just completed group project, telling the teacher what they used (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so she can write a list, and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can listen to an electronic book with a peer and select answers from a picture or word bank to who and what questions about the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, select a book purchased at a recent book fair so the teacher can write down the name and then answer the teacher’s question when she asked, “Do you like the book?,” and place a check in the like column.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so the teacher can add them to the list and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can use a picture/label schedule to identify the next activity of the day by answering what questions (e.g., What is after math? What is next? What is first today?).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences.
I can work with the teacher, identify the centers completed that day and the teacher will write them in the student’s home-school notebook.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, and paper) so the teacher can create a list.
I can with guidance and support, complete open-ended statements about personal experiences when provided with an array of two or more relevant responses (e.g., Playing outside is <fun, hot>).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify personal objects.
I can with guidance and support, select own backpack from two presented at the end of the day which the teacher adds to a chart story (e.g., This sign says Allen. This is Allen’s backpack. This sign says Brian. This is Brian’s backpack.).
I can with guidance and support, select own lunchbox when presented with an array of two or more which the teacher adds to a chart story (e.g., Allen’s lunchbox is blue. Brian’s lunchbox is red.)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.8|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.9|1.text: With guidance and support from adults, recall and use facts from literary and informational text to support reflection and inquiry on characters, setting, key details, specified information, and ideas presented in a text.
WI-CC-ELA|W.1.9|1.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions about characters, settings, and ideas, and explain how these facts support my thinking.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can remember and use facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions about characters, settings, or ideas with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can remember and use simple facts from stories or informational texts to answer questions with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can remember one fact from a story or informational text when someone helps me.
I can talk about the characters or setting of a story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can remember important details from a story or text.
I can retell key information from a story with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say one important thing I remember from a story with support.
I can recall a detail from a story or text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show something I remember from a story.
I can point to something in the book that helps me remember the story with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|W.1.9|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.a|1.text: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups. a. With guidance and support, follow agreed-upon norms for discussions and participate by actively listening, taking turns, and staying on topic.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.a|1.ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in conversations with adults. a. Engage in multiple-turn exchanges with supportive adults.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can participate in discussions by listening carefully, taking turns, and staying on topic without reminders, and help others follow discussion rules.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can follow the rules for discussions by listening, taking turns, and staying on topic with some reminders.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can listen and take turns in a discussion with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can initiate multiple-turn exchanges with peers.
I can during a literacy center activity, hold up own work to show peer and say, “look.” When peer responds, the student continues in the exchange for at least one more turn.
I can when getting ready to read with a partner, initiate an interaction saying, “Read?” The peer responds “Sure, where should we go?” and the student says, “corner” while pointing to the reading corner. The interaction continues so that both students have at least two turns.
I can during snack time, use a multiple message voice output device to say, “Scooby Doo!” and then looks directly at a peer. The peer responds, “Scooby Doo!” The student uses the device to link together, “You - Scooby Doo!” and the peer responds, “No, you - Scooby Doo.” The interaction continues with the two playfully teasing one another.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers.
I can while at a literacy center working with letters and words, participate in multiple-turn exchanges (e.g., one of the peers hands the student a letter and says, “You need this one?” The student replies, “No, b!” The peer finds a b and says, “This one?” The student replies, “Yeah, b.”).
I can when the snack helper asks, “What do you want?” and holds up the white milk and chocolate milk, look directly at the chocolate milk. When the peer acknowledges, “Okay, chocolate,” use sign language to say, “Thank you.” The peer replies, “You’re welcome.”
I can use a sequenced message device to communicate a social script with a peer such as: Student activates switch to say, “Wanna hear a joke?” Peer says “Okay.” Student activates switch to say, “What number does a pig call when he’s in trouble?” Peer says, “I don’t know” and student activates switch to say “Swine 1-1.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can communicate directly with a peer.
I can use a sequenced message device to call students’ names to line up to leave the room.
I can use a single message voice output device to say “hi” to a peer when travelling down the hall.
I can call a peer by name to ask him to come play.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate with a peer.
I can during morning meeting, use a single message voice output device to say, “Good morning” to each classmate when the teacher prompts, “What do you want to say to John?” while pointing to the single message device.
I can during P.E., sit next to the P.E. teacher and use a sequenced message device to call the names of peers in a game like Red Rover. The P.E. teacher prompts by telling when it is time to “Tell them who to send now!”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.a|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.b|1.text: Build on others' talk in conversations by responding to the comments of others through multiple exchanges.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.b|1.ee_text: Build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can add my own thoughts to conversations by responding to what others say and keeping the discussion going with multiple exchanges.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can respond to what others say in conversations and add my own ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add a simple response to what others say in conversations with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can build on comments or topics initiated by an adult and peers.
I can during shared reading, the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!” Another peer comments, “I have a dog like that!” The student adds, “big dog,” and the teacher acknowledges, “Yes, this is a big dog in the picture.”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.
I can during shared reading, when the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!,” the student responds using sign language to communicate, “Me!” The teacher replies, “Me? Do you have a dog?” and the student nods.
I can reply “Sunny?” when an adult comments about the weather saying, “It sure is hot out there. It feels like summer.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, build on comments or topics initiated by an adult.
I can during shared reading, the teacher points to an illustration and comments, “Look at that dog!” Then she says, “You have a dog, don’t you?” The student responds by saying, “Me.” The teacher adds, “I have seen your dog. You have a big dog.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate with an adult about the current topic.
I can during morning meeting, the teacher looks out the window and says, “It looks rainy out there!” then shows the students a picture of rain saying, “This is rain. Look at the picture of rain.” The student looks at the picture of rain.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.b|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.c|1.text: Ask questions to clear up any confusion about the topics and texts under discussion.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.c|1.ee_text: Use one or two words to ask questions related to the topic or text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask questions to make sure I understand everything being discussed and clarify any confusion during conversations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask questions when I don’t understand something in a discussion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask for help if I don’t understand something with support from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can combines three or more words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can during shared reading, point to a page in the book and ask, “What doggie doing?”
I can during literacy centers, use a multiple message communication device to link together words and ask, “What you do?”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use one or two-words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can at lunchtime, use sign to ask for “More?” of a preferred food item.
I can after lunch, ask if they are going outside for recess (i.e., “Go outside?”).
I can select a single picture symbol from a communication display of four or more symbols during a shared reading activity to ask a question (e.g., The message says one of the following: “I have a question,” “Who,” or “Why.”). Teacher responds according to the question (e.g., “Who? Do you want to know who did it? Let’s see.”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use one or two-words to ask questions related to personally relevant topics.
I can during snack time, the student grabs for more crackers but the teacher stops him and supports him in pointing to a picture symbol representing the word more. As the child touches more the teacher says, “Can I have more?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use gestures, vocalizations, symbols, or words to communicate about personally relevant topics.
I can on the playground, vocalize or hit a single message voice output device to signal “go fast” so that someone will push him fast across the yard.
I can during snack time, touch own mouth to indicate a desire for more food.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.c|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.d|1.text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.d|1.ee_text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can adjust how I speak depending on who I am talking to, taking into account others' feelings, needs, or language differences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can think about how others feel or what they need when I speak to them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can show kindness when talking to others with reminders from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can listen to others and share my thoughts when someone helps me.
I can think about how others feel when talking to them with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can listen to others and think about how they feel before talking.
I can communicate with others in a way that is kind and respectful.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can listen to what someone says and respond with help.
I can think about how others feel when I talk with support.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words with help.
I can show care for others when I communicate with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.1.d|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.2|1.text: Ask and answer questions about key details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.2|1.ee_text: During shared reading activities, answer questions about details presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask and answer detailed questions about important parts of a story or information I’ve heard to show I understand.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask and answer questions about important details in a story or information I’ve heard.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can answer simple questions about important details from a story or information I’ve heard with some help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can during shared reading activities, ask and answer questions about key details presented orally or through other media.
I can ask, “What’s that?” in reference to a picture in the book and answers the teacher when she responds, “What do you see?”
I can use a multiple message voice output device to respond to the teacher’s question, “What did the boy do?,” saying, “play.” Then, asks the teacher, “Why?”
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can during shared reading activities, answer questions about details presented orally or through other media.
I can answer yes/no questions about key details presented in a story read aloud.
I can point to a picture in the book to respond when asked a question such as, “Where is the brick house?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support during shared reading activities, provides responses to open-ended statements.
I can after asking the question, “What did the boy see?” and not getting a response, the teacher transforms the question and says, “The boy saw____,” and the student selects a symbol that finishes the sentence.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support during shared reading activities, follow simple directives.
I can during shared reading, reaches out when the teacher comes close, holds out the book, and says, “Turn the page.”
I can during shared reading, the student looks at the illustration when the teacher says, “look” and shines a flashlight on the page.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.2|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.3|1.text: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information or clarify something that is not understood.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.3|1.ee_text: Communicate confusion or lack of understanding ("I don't know.").

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask detailed questions to get more information or to better understand what someone is saying, and answer others' questions with clear explanations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask and answer questions to better understand what someone says.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask simple questions when I don’t understand something with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask for help when needed using words.
I can use communication device, conventional sign, or spoken words to ask for assistance when needed.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask for help when needed.
I can indicate a need for assistance through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can use a switch to gain attention.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, ask for help when needed.
I can when asked, “Do you need help?” respond to indicate need for assistance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, respond to offer of assistance when needed.
I can when teacher offers assistance, respond by attending to teacher.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.3|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.4|1.text: Describe people, places, things, and events with relevant details, expressing ideas clearly.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.4|1.ee_text: Identify familiar people, places, things, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can describe people, places, things, and events with many details to help others understand exactly what I mean.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe people, places, things, and events with details that help others understand my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe people, places, and things with some details with help from my teacher.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify familiar people, places, things, and events.
I can identify people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can identify a photograph or drawing of a birthday party or other event held in the classroom.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support, identify familiar people, places, things, and events.
I can with guidance and support, identify familiar people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can identify a desired objects from choices (e.g., During a before-reading activity, the teacher introduces a number of objects that will be found in the story; during reading, the teacher offers the student a choice of two when the item appears in the book and the student points or gazes to the correct object when asked.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify favorite people and things.
I can with guidance and support, identify a favorite toy or comfort item from a display of two or more.
I can with guidance and support, identify a favorite person by eye contact, eye gaze, vocalizations, etc.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to familiar people, places, things, and events with guidance and support.
I can with guidance and support, respond to familiar people through gestures, eye contact or gaze, vocalizations, etc.
I can with guidance and support, respond to a photo, drawing, or object about a classroom event.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.4|1.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.5|1.text: Create an original or utilize existing visual displays to support descriptions to clarify ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.1.5|1.ee_text: Add or select drawings or other visual or tactile displays that relate to familiar people, places, things, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create my own drawings or use existing pictures to help explain my ideas and make them easier to understand.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use drawings or pictures to help explain my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use pictures or drawings with help to show what I mean.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can combine three or more words, signs, or symbols to communicate own thoughts, feelings, or ideas.
I can when asked “What do you want?,” respond, “I want more.”

I can repeat a word that rhymes when I hear a rhyming word with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.2|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.a|2.text: Know and apply grade-level phonics and word analysis skills in decoding words. a. Distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one- syllable words.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.a|2.ee_text: Demonstrate emerging use of letter-sound knowledge to read words. a. I can identify the lower case letters of the alphabet.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can confidently and consistently distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words. I have a deep understanding of spelling-sound correspondences for a wide range of common vowel teams. I can effortlessly decode and encode a variety of regularly spelled one, two, and three syllable CVC pattern words, and I can apply these skills to read and write more complex words and texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish long and short vowels when reading regularly spelled one-syllable words. I know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams. I can decode and encode regularly spelled one, two, and some three syllable CVC pattern words (e.g., 1 syllable: mat, 2 syllable: picnic, 3 syllable: fantastic, etc.).
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes distinguish between long and short vowels when reading simple one-syllable words. I know a few spelling-sound correspondences for common vowel teams, and with support, I can decode and encode some regularly spelled one, two, and three syllable CVC pattern words.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some vowel sounds in simple one-syllable words, but I struggle to distinguish between long and short vowels. I have limited knowledge of spelling-sound correspondences for common vowel teams, and I have difficulty decoding and encoding regularly spelled one, two, and three syllable CVC pattern words.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can apply letter-sound and word analysis skills in decoding words. In context, identify 18 or more letter-sound associations.
I can when given a sound spoken by an adult during a shared writing activity, say or point to the letter.
I can during a shared reading or writing activity, the teacher points to a letter and the student says the associated sound.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can in context, identify any letter-sound association.
I can when asked to write own name, indicates the sound of the initial letter.
I can during a shared writing activity of an alphabet book, indicates the letter that goes with a sound produced by a teacher.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can explore letter-sound associations.
I can use a talking word processor that provides individual letter name and sound feedback to type.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.b|2.text: Know spelling-sound correspondences for additional common vowel teams.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.b|2.ee_text: Demonstrate emerging use of letter-sound knowledge to read words. b. Identify letter sound correspondence for single consonants.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can recognize and read words with different vowel teams like "ou," "ie," and "oy" easily.
I can apply my knowledge of vowel teams to spell new words without help.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read and spell words with common vowel teams like "oa," "ea," and "ee."
I can use vowel teams in my writing to show long vowel sounds.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read words with vowel teams like "ai" and "ee" with some help.
I can try to spell words with vowel teams when someone supports me.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize a vowel team like "ai" or "ee" when someone shows me.
I can match a vowel team in a word to a long vowel sound with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can say the sound that goes with each consonant letter.
I can match a consonant sound to its correct letter when reading or writing.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say the sound for some consonant letters with help.
I can point to the correct letter when I hear its sound with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize and respond to a consonant sound when I hear it with support.
I can point to or repeat a consonant sound when shown the letter with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.c|2.text: Decode and encode regularly spelled one, two, and some three syllable CVC pattern words (e.g., 1 syllable: mat, 2 syllable: picnic, 3 syllable: fantastic, etc.).

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read and write words with up to three syllables, like "fantastic" and "picnic," using CVC patterns independently.
I can break long words into syllables to help me spell and read them accurately.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read and spell one- and two-syllable words like "mat" and "picnic" using the CVC pattern.
I can break words into syllables to read and write them correctly.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read and spell one-syllable CVC words like "cat" and "dog" with help.
I can break two-syllable words into parts to read and spell them with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize and read short CVC words like "cat" with help.
I can try to spell simple CVC words when someone shows me the pattern.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.d|2.text: Decode words with common prefixes and suffixes.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read and spell words with prefixes like "un-" and "pre-" and suffixes like "-ful" or "-ness" independently.
I can explain how adding a prefix or suffix changes the meaning of a word.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read words with common prefixes and suffixes like "unhappy" or "helpful."
I can understand how adding prefixes and suffixes changes the meaning of a word.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read words with prefixes like "un-" or suffixes like "-ed" with some help.
I can try to use words with prefixes or suffixes in my reading and writing with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize that some words have beginnings or endings like "un-" or "-ing" with help.
I can match a word with a prefix or suffix to its meaning when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.d|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.e|2.text: Decode regularly spelled two- syllable words with long vowels. Encode some of these words. • Know when to drop the final e when adding an -ing, -ed endings. (Silent-e vowel pattern base word). • Know when to double the final consonant when adding a suffix. - ing, -ed.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read and spell two-syllable words with long vowels, like "complete" and "inside," independently.
I can use rules like dropping the final "e" or doubling the consonant when adding endings like "-ing" or "-ed."
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read and spell two-syllable words with long vowels, like "eagle" and "broken."
I know when to drop the final "e" or double the consonant when adding "-ing" or "-ed."
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read two-syllable words with long vowels with help and try to spell them.
I can try to add "-ing" or "-ed" to words with help, but I may need support to follow the rules.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize two-syllable words with long vowels when someone shows me.
I can try to spell long vowel words when someone helps me with the rules.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.e|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.f|2.text: Recognize and read grade- appropriate irregularly spelled words.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.f|2.ee_text: Demonstrate emerging use of letter-sound knowledge to read words. f. Recognize 10 or more written words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can confidently recognize and read a wide range of grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words. I can apply my knowledge of these words to fluently read and comprehend more complex texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize and read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recognize and read some grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words with support, but my knowledge is limited.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some common sight words, but I struggle to recognize and read most grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize 10 or more written words.
I can when asked, reads 10 or more words on the classroom word wall (can point to words as they teacher calls them or reads them orally).
I can when given a list of familiar consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words, successfully reads 10 or more words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize two or more written words.
I can point to the correct word when read by someone else.
I can match written word to an object.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize symbols that represent two or more common words.
I can recognize symbols that are part of the daily schedule.
I can recognize symbols that represent lunch item choices.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.3.f|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.a|2.text: Read with sufficient accuracy and fluency to support comprehension. a. Read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.a|2.ee_text: Attend to words in print. a. Read familiartext comprised of known words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently read a wide range of grade-level texts with a deep level of purpose and understanding. My oral reading is consistently accurate, with an appropriate rate and expressive delivery. I can seamlessly use context to quickly confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, and I rarely need to reread.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can read grade-level text with purpose and understanding. I can read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings. I can use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can read some grade-level texts with basic purpose and understanding. My oral reading is somewhat accurate, with an appropriate rate and some expression. I can sometimes use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding, but I may need to reread frequently.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can read some simple grade-level texts, but I often lack purpose and understanding. My oral reading is inaccurate and lacks appropriate rate and expression. I struggle to use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize 10 or more written words.
I can when asked, reads 10 or more words on the classroom word wall (can point to words as they teacher calls them or reads them orally).
I can when given a list of familiar consonant-vowel-consonant (CVC) words, successfully reads 10 or more words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize two or more written words.
I can point to the correct word when read by someone else.
I can match written word to an object.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize symbols that represent two or more common words.
I can recognize symbols that are part of the daily schedule.
I can recognize symbols that represent lunch item choices.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.b|2.text: Read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read a text aloud smoothly, with the right speed and expression, without help.
I can improve my fluency each time I reread a text, sounding more like natural speech.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text aloud with good speed and expression.
I can read a text more accurately and with better expression when I practice reading it again.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read aloud with some expression and at a good speed with guidance.
I can read better and more smoothly after practicing a text several times.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can read aloud with help and improve my reading speed when someone supports me.
I can practice reading a text and get better each time with guidance.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.c|2.text: Use context to confirm or self- correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.c|2.ee_text: With support, monitor for and identify errors that disrupt comprehension

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use the context in a sentence to figure out or correct difficult words without help.
I can reread parts of a text on my own to understand and correct my reading mistakes.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use context clues to figure out or fix a word when reading.
I can reread parts of a text to help me understand words and meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use clues from the text to help me understand or fix words when someone guides me.
I can reread parts of a text with help to make sure I understand it.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use help to understand or fix a word I don’t know while reading.
I can reread parts of a story or text when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recognize when I make a mistake while reading and fix it with help.
I can check if what I read makes sense and ask for help if I don’t understand.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can notice when something I read doesn’t sound right and ask for help.
I can correct a mistake in reading with guidance when someone helps me notice it.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can stop when I don’t understand something while reading and ask for help with support.
I can recognize when a word I read doesn’t match the story with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.2.4.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.1|2.text: Develop and answer questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.1|2.ee_text: hen given guidance and support, answer “who”, “what” and “where” questions in familiar texts. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and thoughtfully develop a range of questions to deeply explore and demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I can analyze important information, explain the central message or theme, and make insightful connections, inferences, and intertextual links.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and answer questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I can identify important information, explain the main message or events, and make relevant connections.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can develop and answer some basic questions about key ideas and details in a text, but my understanding is limited. I can identify a few important details, but I have trouble explaining the main message or events.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty developing and answering questions to demonstrate an understanding of key ideas and details in a text. I struggle to identify important information and understand the main message or events.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can answer who and what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a familiar text.
I can when given a set of familiar directions, answer questions about who follows the directions and what is one thing to do to complete the task.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can answer what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a text.
I can when given the instructions for a model plane/car, birdhouse, or other craft project, identify what would happen if they did not use glue (or another key ingredient).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and supports, identify a detail in a text or illustration.
I can Shown a calendar, point to any date.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.1|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.2|2.text: Summarize portions of a text in order to identify a main topic or central idea and key details in a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.2|2.ee_text: Identify the topic of a text (RI) and use details to recount events from familiar stories (RL).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and coherently summarize portions of a text, accurately identifying the main topic or central idea and carefully selecting and explaining the most salient supporting details. My summaries demonstrate a deep comprehension of the text and an ability to discern the most important information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize portions of a text in order to identify a main topic or central idea and key details in a text. I can concisely capture the essential information and explain how the details support the main idea.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can summarize some portions of a text, but I have trouble consistently identifying the main topic or central idea and the most important supporting details. My summaries may be incomplete or lack focus.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to summarize portions of a text in order to identify the main topic or central idea and key details. I have difficulty distinguishing important information from less relevant details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the topic of the text.
I can From three options, identify the topic of a series of directions (e.g., Would the title be Making a Cake, Building a Birdhouse, or Riding the Bus?).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can retell the title of a text.
I can after reading the title and steps for a series of directions, repeat the title.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
