I can indicate a portion of a text.
I can when given a set of directions, point to any step or the title.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.2|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.3|2.text: Describe how characters respond to major events and challenges. (RL) Describe the connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.3|2.ee_text: Identify the actions of characters (RL) or important details and events (RI) in familiar and unfamiliar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can thoroughly and insightfully describe how characters respond to major events and challenges, analyzing their motivations, emotions, and character development.
I can expertly describe complex connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text, demonstrating a deep comprehension of the relationships and their significance.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can describe how characters respond to major events and challenges in a story, explaining their motivations and reactions.
I can describe the connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can describe how characters respond to some major events and challenges, but my explanations may be incomplete or lack depth.
I can identify and describe some connections between ideas, concepts, or a series of events in an informational text, but my understanding is still developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I have difficulty describing how characters respond to major events and challenges in a story. I struggle to identify the characters' motivations and reactions.
I can identify some basic connections between ideas, concepts, or events in an informational text, but I have trouble explaining the relationships in detail.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify the actions and feelings of the characters in a familiar story.
I can during shared reading sessions, share with peers how characters feel in a familiar story? “How does the pig feel when the wolf says, ‘I will huff and puff and blow your house down?’”
I can during shared reading sessions, will share with peers what characters did and how that made them feel (e.g., “How did the wolf get into the brick house and how did that make the pig feel?”).
I can when given an array of symbols, selects a symbol that reflects the characters’ feelings on each page of a familiar story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with prompting, identify the actions and feeling of characters in a familiar story.
I can With prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, tell what characters are doing on each page.
I can with prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, act out feelings or actions of the characters in the story.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with prompting, identify a character in a familiar story.
I can when given an array of pictures of characters from the book and classmates, chooses a picture of the character in the story.
I can With prompting during shared reading of a familiar story, use a two location voice output device programmed with happy and sad to label the feelings of characters in the story.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.3|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.4|2.text: Explain how specific words and phrases express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific words within a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.4|2.ee_text: Use a text’s structure (e.g., repetition, rhyming, etc.) to identify specific content, sensory, or feeling words that meaningfully relate to the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully explain how the author's strategic use of specific words and phrases in a text express complex emotions, vividly appeal to the senses, and provide essential context for understanding content-specific vocabulary. I can make sophisticated connections between the language use and the text's meaning, tone, and effect on the reader
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific words. I can analyze the impact of the author's language choices on the reader's understanding and experience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some ways that specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or provide context for understanding content-specific vocabulary, but my explanations are basic and lack depth.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty explaining how specific words and phrases in a text express feelings, appeal to the senses, or determine the meaning of content-specific vocabulary. I struggle to analyze the impact of language on the reader's understanding.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify words that describe feelings or senses in a text that uses rhyming or repetition.
I can find important words that help me understand a story’s structure, like repeated or rhyming words.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize rhyming or repeating words in a story with help.
I can find one word that shows a feeling or idea in a text with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen for a word that sounds the same or repeats in a story with support.
I can point to or say a word that describes something I hear or feel in the text with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.4|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.5|2.text: Describe the overall structure of a text, including describing how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes the text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.5|2.ee_text: Identify the beginning and end of a familiar sequential text (RL) or identify relevant graphics in an informational text (RI).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully describe the complex structure of a text, expertly explaining how the beginning effectively introduces the topic, theme, or narrative, and the ending powerfully concludes it. I can analyze the author's strategic use of organizational elements and their impact on the text's meaning and impact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe the overall structure of a text, including how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes it. I can analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the text's organizational choices.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can describe some basic elements of a text's structure, but I have trouble fully explaining how the beginning introduces the text and the ending concludes it. My understanding of the text's organization is still developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty describing the overall structure of a text, including how the beginning and ending sections function. I struggle to identify key organizational features and the connections between different parts of the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell where a story begins and ends in a book I know.
I can find pictures or graphics that give important information in an informational text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can show where a story starts or finishes with help.
I can find one important graphic in an informational text with some guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to the first or last part of a story with support.
I can point to a picture or graphic that goes with a story or information with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.5|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.6|2.text: I can identify examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of the text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.6|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, identify words and graphic representations that connect to the point of view, topic, or important details of the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully identify a wide range of examples demonstrating how the strategic use of illustrations, text features, and details powerfully support and enhance the point of view or purpose of a text. I can make sophisticated connections between the visual and textual elements, and analyze their collective impact on the reader's understanding and experience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify multiple examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of a text. I can explain how these elements contribute to the overall meaning and effectiveness of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic examples of how illustrations, text features, and details relate to the point of view or purpose of a text, but my understanding is still developing. I may not be able to fully explain the connections or their significance.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty identifying examples of how illustrations, text features, and details support the point of view or purpose of a text. I struggle to make connections between the visual and textual elements and the overall meaning or message.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can find words or pictures in a text that show the main idea or a character’s point of view.
I can identify words and images that are important to understanding the story or topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find one word or picture that shows how a character feels or what the story is about with help.
I can recognize one important word or image in the text with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture or say a word that shows what the story or topic is about with support.
I can identify a word or picture related to the main idea with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.6|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.7|2.text: Demonstrate understanding of story elements and/or topics by applying information gained from illustrations or text features. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.7|2.ee_text: Identify illustrations or objects/tactile information in text that depict characters. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully demonstrate a deep understanding of complex story elements and/or topics by expertly applying a wide range of detailed information gained from the strategic use of illustrations and text features. I can make sophisticated, nuanced connections that enhance my interpretation and analysis of the text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can demonstrate a clear understanding of story elements and/or topics by effectively applying relevant information gained from illustrations and text features. I can make thoughtful connections between the visual/textual details and my overall comprehension of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can demonstrate a basic understanding of some story elements or topics by applying information gained from illustrations or text features, but my connections may be limited or lack depth
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty demonstrating understanding of story elements or topics by using information from illustrations or text features. I struggle to connect visual and textual details to my overall comprehension of the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use illustrations in print or digital text to identify characters and settings.
I can when given three illustrations, select the one that depicts the setting in the story.
I can find an illustration in the book that shows a specified character.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find the character in an illustration from a familiar text.
I can during shared reading of a familiar text when the teacher stops at a page with an illustration that includes a specified character, point to the character.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can attend to illustrations in the text during shared reading.
I can visually attend to the illustration when the teacher holds up the book for the student to see.
I can visually attend to the book during shared reading.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.7|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.8|2.text: Explain how specific points the author or illustrator makes in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.8|2.ee_text: Identify points the author makes in text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully explain how the author's or illustrator's specific, complex points in an informational text are powerfully supported by a rich array of relevant, well-chosen reasons and evidence. I can make sophisticated, nuanced connections that demonstrate a deep understanding of the author's or illustrator's purpose and the impact of the supporting information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can clearly explain how the specific points made by the author or illustrator in an informational text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. I can analyze the purpose and effectiveness of the supporting information in strengthening the author's or illustrator's claims.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic connections between the specific points made by the author or illustrator and the supporting reasons and evidence, but my explanations are limited. I may not fully understand the purpose or significance of the supporting details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty explaining how the specific points made by the author or illustrator in an informational text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. I struggle to identify and analyze the connections between the claims and the supporting information.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell one or two important points the author makes in a text.
I can explain what the author wants me to know about the topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or point to one important point the author makes with guidance.
I can recognize one key idea the author gives in the text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond when asked about an important point the author makes with support.
I can point to or say one thing the author talks about with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.8|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.9|2.text: Compare and contrast key points or perspectives presented in two texts; recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.2.9|2.ee_text: Compare details in two texts; recognize that texts reflect one’s own and other’s culture. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly and insightfully compare and contrast the complex, nuanced key points and perspectives presented in two texts. I can make sophisticated, well-supported connections between the texts and their reflections of one's own and others' cultures, demonstrating a deep understanding of how cultural influences shape the content and portrayal of information and narratives.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively compare and contrast the key points or perspectives presented in two texts. I can also recognize how the texts may reflect the author's or characters' cultural backgrounds and experiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify some basic similarities and differences between the key points or perspectives in two texts, but my comparisons are limited. I may not fully understand how texts can reflect cultural influences.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty comparing and contrasting the key points or perspectives presented in two texts. I also struggle to recognize that texts can reflect one's own and others' cultures.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can tell how details from two texts are the same or different.
I can explain how stories reflect different cultures, including my own.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can find one detail that is the same or different in two stories with help.
I can recognize one thing that shows a story is from a different culture with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say something that is the same or different in two stories with support.
I can use pictures or words to show something about a story from another culture with help.

WI-CC-ELA|R.2.9|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.1|2.text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.1|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can expertly compose sophisticated, nuanced examples of reflective, formal, and creative writing that seamlessly address a wide array of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes. I can fluidly integrate these various modes of writing and demonstrate a deep understanding of how to strategically compose for different objectives and audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compose reflective, formal, and creative writing that serves a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes. I can effectively address the appropriate objectives and integrate these different modes of writing as needed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can compose some basic examples of reflective, formal, and creative writing, but my ability to do so for a range of purposes is limited. I may have difficulty balancing high-stakes and low-stakes objectives in my writing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty composing reflective, formal, and creative writing for a variety of purposes. I struggle to produce writing that effectively addresses high-stakes or low-stakes objectives.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a book and write, draw, or dictate to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, use a multiple message communication device to say, “good book” and then add a reason, “funny.”
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, draw a picture of a sad face to show that he or she doesn’t like it and then ask the teacher to write “too hard” under the picture.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a book and write, draw, or dictate to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, then the teacher will navigate through the student’s multiple message communication device to reveal messages that express an opinion, then select a message communicating an opinion (e.g., “It’s really good!”). The teacher asks, “What makes it good?,” and the student will use the device to answer (e.g., says “boy”) which the teacher interprets to mean the student liked the main character who was a boy.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, state an opinion about a book.
I can look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite,” which the teacher writes (e.g., Maria’s favorite is Goodnight Moon.).
I can after the media specialist shows the students two books they might want to check out, look at one of them and indicate a preference (e.g., smiles).

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.1|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.a|2.text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which they introduce the topic or text they are writing about; state an opinion; supply reasons that support the opinion using words for emphasis, addition, contrast, or order to connect opinion and reasons; and provide a concluding statement or section.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.a|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write sophisticated, nuanced examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, expertly using the required elements and structure for each mode. My writing demonstrates a thorough understanding of how to effectively introduce topics/texts, state opinions with well-chosen supporting reasons, use facts and details to develop points, and provide meaningful, cohesive conclusions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write proficient examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, incorporating the necessary elements and structure for each mode. My writing introduces topics/texts, states opinions with supporting reasons, uses facts and details to develop points, and provides appropriate conclusions.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write some basic examples of opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives, but my ability to effectively use the required elements and structure for each mode is limited. My writing may lack cohesion or development.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to write text in a variety of modes, including opinion pieces, informative/explanatory text, and narratives. I have difficulty introducing topics, stating opinions, using supporting reasons and details, and providing appropriate conclusions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose a message with one fact about the topic.
I can select a topic based on a bulletin board in the classroom about life cycles, then draw a picture of a frog, tell a peer to write frog next to the picture or add a picture of a tadpole and writes tp.
I can look through a photo album parents have sent in from home and select a picture of the beach and then dictate a fact about the picture for the teacher to write: “The beach is hot.” or “The beach has water.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic and use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose a message with one fact about a topic.
I can when given a familiar topic such as a favorite TV show, draw a picture of a character in the show and complete a frame sentence using a word bank: “<Name of character> is <one fact>.” (e.g., “Barney is purple.” or “Barney is happy.”).
I can when given a topic from a recently completed classroom activity, within a small group tell the teacher one thing that happened during the activity as the teacher writes a repeated line of text, One thing we did was . . . . Another thing we did was . . . . We also did . . . .
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic.
I can Working with a group of peers, select the topic each peer will write about from a choice of two or more.
I can Select the topic for a shared writing activity from two or more choices offered by the teacher.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.b|2.text: Informative or explanatory text in which they introduce a topic, use facts and definitions to develop points, and provide a concluding statement or section.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.b|2.ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they provide at least 1 fact about a predetermined or self chosen topic

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can independently write an informative text that introduces a topic, uses clear facts, and ends with a strong conclusion.
I can connect facts and definitions in my writing to fully explain a topic.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write an informative text that introduces a topic, uses facts, and provides a clear conclusion.
I can use definitions and facts to explain the points I make in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write a simple informative text with some facts and a conclusion, with help.
I can try to include facts and definitions in my writing, with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can introduce a topic and include one fact in my writing, with help.
I can add a sentence to finish my writing when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or say one fact about a topic I know.
I can give one important piece of information about a chosen topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can give a simple fact about a topic with help.
I can say one thing I know about a topic with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to or say a word about a topic I know with support.
I can share information using pictures or words with help.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.c|2.text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narratives in which they recount a well elaborated event or short sequence of events; include details to describe actions, thoughts, and feelings; and use temporal words to signal event order, and provide a sense of closure.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.c|2.ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write a detailed narrative that describes actions, thoughts, and feelings, using temporal words to clearly order events and bring the story to a satisfying close.
I can write a story with rich details that show how characters feel and what they are thinking.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write a narrative with details that describe actions, thoughts, and feelings, using temporal words like "first" and "then" to order events and provide a conclusion.
I can tell a story that shows what characters are doing and feeling.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write about a sequence of events using some details and temporal words like "next" and "after," with help.
I can try to describe what characters do or feel in my story with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about one or two events in order using simple words like "first" or "then," with help.
I can try to describe what happened in my story with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can write or talk about something that happened, including details about what happened.
I can tell a story about one event or several events that are linked together.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or write about one event from a story or my own experience with some help.
I can share a few details about what happened with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can point to a picture or say a word about something that happened with support.
I can use pictures or words to show what happened in one part of a story with help.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.2.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.a|2.text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Provide a beginning, middle and ending that works cohesively to promote the central theme of the text.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.a|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses words familiar to the student and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create sophisticated, nuanced writing that expertly organizes a complex, central theme with a seamlessly cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I use a variety of well-chosen transitions to build strong, sophisticated connections between ideas and events. I demonstrate a command of descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide rich, vivid examples that enhance the overall effectiveness of the writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create writing that effectively organizes a central theme with a cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I use transitions to link ideas and events, and incorporate descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide vivid details and examples.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can create some basic writing that attempts to organize a central theme and use transitions and descriptive vocabulary, but my execution is limited. My writing may lack cohesion or fully developed ideas, details, and connections.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to create writing that effectively organizes a central theme with a cohesive beginning, middle, and ending. I also have difficulty using transitions to connect ideas and events, and incorporating descriptive, domain-specific vocabulary to provide vivid details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select an event or personal experience and use drawing, writing, or dictating to compose a message about it.
I can draw a picture about his or her brother’s soccer game, asks the teacher to write his or her brother’s name, and then signs own name to the picture.
I can look through digital photos that the teacher took while the children completed a class project, select a photo and dictate a message for the teacher to write.
I can following an in-class cooking experience, name the activity (e.g., “Mkg Ckes” [Making Cookies]), describing what was done (e.g., “Mak sgr ckz” [We make sugar cookies.]), describing how it felt (e.g., “Do stke” [The dough was sticky.]), and telling how they liked it (e.g., “Likem.” [I liked them.]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can draw, write, or dictate to compose a message about a personal experience.
I can tell the teacher about a trip to the pet shop and draw a picture of it when asked.
I can when the teacher displays a picture of the student working with peers to complete a class project, dictate a message to go with it.
I can following an in-class cooking experience, use a teacher-provided template to name the activity (e.g., “Mkg Ckez” [Making Cookies]), and tell how they liked it (e.g., “Likem.” [I liked them.]).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate about a personal experience.
I can after the teacher talked with the student about going to an activity (e.g., his or her brother’s soccer game) and asks, “Was it good?” The student indicates answer (e.g., indicate no by looking down) and the teacher writes in the student’s journal (e.g., Tamika went to her brother’s soccer game. It was not fun.).
I can after the teacher works with the student to review the events in his or her schedule for the day, points to and labels each of the visual supports, and asks, “Did you do it?” The student indicates an answer (e.g., indicate yes by smiling), and the teacher writes Brian did art, in his home-school journal.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.b|2.text: Transitions: use transitions to link and build connections between ideas, text, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use a variety of transitions to smoothly connect ideas and events in my writing.
I can choose transitions that make my writing flow naturally and clearly.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use transitions like "because," "then," and "next" to connect ideas and events in my writing.
I can make my writing flow better by using simple transitions.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use basic transitions like "and" or "then" to link ideas and events, with some support.
I can try to connect events in my writing with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use simple words like "and" or "next" to connect ideas in my writing, with help.
I can try to link two ideas in my writing with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.c|2.text: Word Choice (including domain specific): use descriptive words to demonstrate creativity and to providevivid examples of feelings, events, and images.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use creative and descriptive words to vividly describe characters’ feelings, actions, and settings in my writing.
I can paint a clear picture with words to help readers imagine the events in my story.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use descriptive words to show how characters feel or what is happening in my writing.
I can describe events and images in my story using words that help readers understand.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use a few descriptive words to describe characters’ feelings or actions, with some support.
I can try to use words that make my story clearer with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can try to use simple words to describe how someone feels or what happens in my writing, with help.
I can name feelings or describe an event in basic terms with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.3.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.4|2.text: I can with guidance and support from adults, produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task and purpose. (Grade- specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write about a topic in a way that reflects my culture and is authentic to the task, without help.
I can organize and develop my writing to show who I am and what is important to me.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can write about a topic that shows my culture or experiences, and organize my ideas clearly, with some guidance.
I can make sure my writing matches the task and purpose with help.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write about something important to me, and with support, make sure it fits the task and purpose.
I can try to organize my writing and include details about my experiences with help.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write about my ideas or culture with help, and organize my writing with support from an adult.
I can get help to make my writing match the task or purpose, while sharing something about my experiences.
descriptors.ee_at_target: (Begins in grade 3)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.4|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.5|2.text: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, focus on a topic and strengthen writing as needed by revising and editing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.5|2.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, focus their own drawing, dictation, or writing on a topic and add more details to strengthen their drawing, dictation, or writing as needed.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can with minimal guidance and support, I can independently focus on a topic and masterfully strengthen my writing through sophisticated revision and editing. I demonstrate a deep understanding of the revision and editing process, and can make strategic, well-informed decisions to significantly improve the focus, organization, content, and mechanics of my writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, I can focus on a topic and successfully strengthen my writing by revising and editing as needed. I am able to make meaningful improvements to the focus, organization, content, and mechanics of my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can focus on a topic and make some attempts to revise and edit my writing, but I require significant guidance and support from adults and peers to do so effectively. My revisions and edits may be limited in scope or impact.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty focusing on a topic and strengthening my writing through the revision and editing process, even with guidance and support from adults and peers.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing to strengthen the message.
I can add information created in science center and add information with peer assistance (e.g., The student shares a picture he or she has drawn of the leaves in a science center with some peers. The peers point out details on the leaves and suggest that the student adds the details to the picture and he or she does.).
I can dictate a sentence for the teacher to write. when the teacher asks for clarification (e.g., “Tell me when that happened.”), dictates more to clarify.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults or peers, add more information to own drawing, dictating, or writing when asked.
I can add information to drawing with peer assistance (e.g., The student shares a picture he or she has drawn with some peers when they make suggestions that he or she add more and the student adds more random marks to the picture.).
I can dictate a sentence for the teacher to write. when the teacher asks, “Tell me more,” adds more.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults or peers, use drawing, communication, or writing tools to communicate a message.
I can use a single message voice output device to tell a peer, “Read it to me.” while students are sharing group writing and when invited to contribute his ideas, makes marks on the paper.
I can use a computer-based paint program to draw about a favored activity.
I can select keys on an alternate keyboard to write a note to a friend.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.5|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.6|2.text: I can with guidance and support from adults, use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming most printed upper- and lower-case letters), cursive, or typing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.6|2.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology (including assistive technologies) to produce and publish writing. Learn to produce writing through printing (including forming upper and lower case letters).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can with minimal guidance, I can independently and skillfully use a wide range of digital tools to produce and publish sophisticated, collaborative writing. I have mastered producing writing through printing, cursive, and typing, and can fluidly switch between these methods as needed.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults, I can use a variety of digital tools to effectively produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. I have learned to produce writing through printing, cursive, and typing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some guidance and support from adults, I can use a limited range of digital tools to produce and publish basic writing, sometimes in collaboration with peers. My ability to consistently produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing is developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to use digital tools to produce and publish writing, even with guidance and support from adults. I also have difficulty learning to produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology (including assistive technologies) to produce and publish writing.
I can use an alternative keyboard preprogrammed by the teacher with words and phrases to write a response to a book to publish in the class’ book of book reviews.
I can work with a peer to choose words from word banks and spell words to write about himself or herself for inclusion in a class book, when We Were Babies.
I can with guidance and support, use assistive technology to write back and forth with a parent volunteer in a digital written conversation environment (e.g., e-mail, text message).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, use technology to produce writing.
I can work with a peer, use an alternative keyboard preprogrammed by the teacher with words and phrases to write about a book.
I can work with a peer to choose words from word banks and spell words to write about himself or herself.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, explore writing technologies.
I can take turns selecting preprogrammed messages from an alternative keyboard and listen as the message is read/typed by a talking word processing program.
I can use a single switch with scanning to select letters of the alphabet on an onscreen keyboard.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.6|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.7|2.text: Participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects (e.g., read a number of books on a single topic to produce a report; record science observations).
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.7|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can eagerly participate in complex, sophisticated shared and independent inquiry and writing projects. I can thoroughly research multiple sources, meticulously record detailed observations, and skillfully synthesize the information to produce an exceptional, cohesive written piece.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can actively participate in shared and independent inquiry and writing projects. I can read multiple sources on a topic, record relevant observations, and use the information to produce a well-organized report or other written product.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can participate in some basic shared and independent inquiry and writing projects, but my participation is limited. I may have trouble reading multiple sources, organizing information, and producing a cohesive written piece.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to participate in shared or independent inquiry and writing projects. I have difficulty reading multiple sources on a topic, recording observations, and using the information to produce a report or other written product.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can participate in shared writing projects - communicate a message to add information.
I can select a book on a topic related to a shared research project from a collection identified by peers and identify pictures that relate to the topic being researched, share them, and have peers write and read aloud text to accompany them.
I can read and listen with a peer to two electronic books selected by the teacher in a digital reading environment and with a keyboard with alphabet and whole word access type letters, words, or sentences about what they learn (e.g., Katz r mamls. Bab catz r kitns. [Cats are mammals. Baby cats are kittens.]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, participate in shared writing and research projects.
I can with guidance and support from the teacher, select a book from a choice of two related to the shared research project and identifies pictures that relate to the topic being researched which a peer writes on the collaborative document and reads aloud.
I can when given a premade set-up on an alternative keyboard or onscreen keyboard, select words and pictures to add to a shared research and writing project.
I can type letters as they are dictated by a peer to add content to a shared writing project and then dictate known letters to a peer to type in order to add content to a shared writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select pictures, words, or objects related to a shared research project.
I can when given a multimedia presentation of words and pictures related to a shared research project, use a switch to advance through the pictures looking and/or listening to the words and pictures and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project.
I can use a touchscreen to scroll through pictures related to the topic of a shared research project and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project and read aloud.
I can explore a bin full of objects and artifacts related to a shared research project and select one, which a peer, aide, or teacher will write in the shared research project.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.7|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.8|2.text: Recall information from experiences or gather information from provided sources to answer a question.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.8|2.ee_text: Identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently and comprehensively recall detailed information from a wide range of personal experiences, and expertly gather and synthesize information from multiple provided sources to answer complex questions in-depth.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively recall information from my own experiences and gather relevant information from provided sources to answer questions thoroughly and accurately.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can partially recall information from experiences or gather some information from provided sources to answer basic questions, but my responses may be limited in detail or depth.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty recalling information from my own experiences or gathering information from provided sources to answer questions. My responses are often incomplete or inaccurate.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can identify from a list of things that happened on a field trip to answer questions (e.g., The teacher gives small groups of children a list of questions to answer about a field trip, peers read the questions one-at-a-time, make a list of what they remember, ask the student to identify which things he or she remembers, and then use that information to answer the questions.).
I can after the teacher prepares a set-up on an interactive whiteboard for students to use in recoding their experiences from a science project, identify the pictures that reflect what happened and then move them to the correct location to respond to the teacher’s questions.
I can use a picture/label schedule to recall the activities of the day and answer the question, “What did you do today?” for their parents in the home/school journal.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and answer simple questions about those experiences.
I can work with the teacher, select a book purchased at a recent book fair so the teacher can write down the name and then answer the teacher’s question when she asked, “Do you like the book?” Then, place a check in the like column.
I can work with a small group and the teacher, identify supplies from those assembled on the table that were used in completing a group project (e.g., glue, tape, scissors, paper) so the teacher can add them to the list and then respond to the teacher’s question when she asks, “Did you finish?”
I can use a picture/label schedule to identify the next activity of the day by answering what questions (e.g., What is after math? What is next? What is first today?).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults, identify information related to personal experiences and preferences.
I can work with the teacher, identify a picture of a center completed earlier in the day to answer yes or no to the question, “Did you <listen to a story> this morning?” after which, the teacher will write in the home-school journal, “Allison listened to a story this morning.”
I can work with a small group of peers and the teacher, identify objects and artifacts from a personal experience that will then be labeled appropriately by the teacher (e.g., Science things: rocks, leaves, twigs).

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.8|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.9|2.text: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, recall and use facts from literary and informational text to support reflection and inquiry on characters, setting, key details, specified information, and ideas presented in a text.
WI-CC-ELA|W.2.9|2.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and skillfully recall and use a wide range of relevant facts from literary and informational texts to engage in deep, sophisticated reflection and inquiry about complex characters, settings, key details, specified information, and central ideas. I demonstrate a nuanced understanding of the texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, I can effectively recall and use relevant facts from literary and informational texts to thoughtfully reflect on and inquire about characters, settings, key details, specified information, and central ideas presented in the texts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some guidance and support, I can partially recall and use a few relevant facts from literary and informational texts to reflect on and inquire about basic elements like characters, settings, and key details. However, my responses may be limited in depth and scope.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to recall and use facts from literary and informational texts, even with guidance and support from adults and peers. I have difficulty reflecting on and inquiring about characters, settings, key details, and ideas presented in texts.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can remember and tell important details from a story or informational text.
I can explain key information from a text with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say one important thing I remember from a text with support.
I can recall one detail from a story or informational text with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can use pictures or words to show something I remember from a text with support.
I can point to something in the book that helps me remember details with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|W.2.9|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.a|2.text: Participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about topics and texts with peers and adults in small and larger groups. a. Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions and participate by actively listening, taking turns, gaining the floor in respectful ways, and staying on topic.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.a|2.ee_text: With guidance and support, participate in conversations with adults and peers. a. Engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers with support from an adult.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I consistently and skillfully participate in substantive, collaborative conversations with a wide range of diverse partners. I take a leading role in discussions about complex topics and texts, seamlessly engaging with both small groups and larger audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can actively participate in collaborative conversations with diverse partners about a variety of topics and texts, both in small groups and larger settings. I engage thoughtfully with my peers and adults.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With some support, I can participate in basic collaborative conversations about topics and texts, but my participation may be limited or uneven. I can engage with a few diverse partners in small groups, but have more difficulty in larger group settings.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty participating in collaborative conversations, even with guidance and support. I struggle to engage with diverse partners about topics and texts in both small and larger group settings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers and adults in small groups.
I can after shared reading of a fable in a small group, take turns talking about the fable with the teacher’s involvement.
I can during lunchtime, communicate about the weekend taking multiple turns with peers and adults who are sitting at the table.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with individual peers.
I can while at a literacy center working with letters and words when a peer hands the student a letter and says, “You need this one?,” and the student replies, “No, b!” The peer finds a letter b and says, “This one?” The student replies, “Yeah, b.”
I can when the snack helper asks, “What do you want?” and holds up the white milk and chocolate milk, look directly at the chocolate milk. The peer acknowledges, “Okay, chocolate.” and the student uses sign language to say, “Thank you.” The peer replies, “You’re welcome.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate directly with an adult.
I can select from an array of pictures to indicate a favorite character in a story.
I can look at the carton of chocolate milk when a teacher holds up a carton of white milk and a carton of chocolate milk and asks, “What do you want?”
I can hand a teacher a picture of a desired toy to request an object during center time.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.b|2.text: Build on others' talk in conversations by linking their comments to the remarks of others.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.b|2.ee_text: Build on others’ talk in conversations

descriptors.cc_advanced: I masterfully build on the talk of others in conversations, seamlessly linking my comments to the evolving discussion in a way that advances the dialogue and demonstrates a deep understanding of my conversation partners' remarks.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively build on the talk of others in conversations by thoughtfully connecting my comments to the previous remarks made by my conversation partners.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes build on the talk of others in conversations, but I may have trouble consistently linking my comments to the previous remarks made. My contributions may be limited or lack cohesion.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty building on the comments of others during conversations. I struggle to make connections between my own remarks and the previous statements made by my conversation partners.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can add my own ideas when someone else is talking in a conversation.
I can respond to others and continue a conversation with help.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can add a comment or ask a question when someone else is talking with some help.
I can share my thoughts after listening to someone else with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words during a conversation with help.
I can show I am listening and add a simple comment with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.c|2.text: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.c|2.ee_text: Ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts under discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I confidently and proactively ask thoughtful, targeted questions to get clarification and deeper explanation about the complex topics and texts under discussion, showing a strong desire to fully comprehend the subject matter.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I appropriately ask for clarification and further explanation as needed about the topics and texts being discussed, in order to deepen my understanding.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I sometimes ask for clarification or further explanation about the topics and texts under discussion, but I may not do so consistently or with enough specificity to get the information I need.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I rarely ask for clarification or further explanation about the topics and texts being discussed, even when I am unsure or need more information.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask questions related to a prescribed topic or text.
I can during shared reading of a fable, ask “What is that?” (pointing to the tortoise).
I can use a multiple message voice output device to ask, “Who?” when the teacher explains that the class will have a special visitor coming to class today.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, ask questions related to a prescribed topic or text.
I can when given a choice of two questions recorded on single message voice output device (e.g., “What happens next?” and “”Why did she do that?”) and support from the teacher who models by saying, “I wonder what will happen next.” or “I wonder why she did that.,” select a question to ask.
I can ask, “How are you today?” during morning group, after several students have asked the question, “How are you today?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use question words (who, what, when, where, why, or how) to communicate with others.
I can when given a single message voice output device with the single word, why during a shared reading activity with an informational text, hit the switch to say “why?”
I can during morning meeting time when the teacher is explaining the calendar to the group, she exaggerates when asking, “Do you know what we’re going to do then?,” the student hits a single message voice output device to say, “What?”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.d|2.text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.d|2.ee_text: Consider individual differences when communicating with others.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I seamlessly integrate consideration of individual differences into all of my communications. I expertly tailor my style, content, and approach to effectively engage with a wide range of individuals, showing a nuanced understanding of diverse perspectives and communication needs.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I consistently consider individual differences when communicating with others. I demonstrate sensitivity to diverse perspectives, backgrounds, and communication needs, and I adjust my approach accordingly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can somewhat consider individual differences when communicating, but my awareness and application of this skill is limited. I may occasionally adjust my communication style or content, but not consistently.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty considering individual differences when communicating with others. My interactions may lack sensitivity or awareness of others' perspectives, backgrounds, and communication needs.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can communicate with others while being respectful of their differences.
I can change how I talk to others depending on their needs or feelings.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can think about how others feel when I talk to them with guidance.
I can communicate with others, thinking about their feelings, with help.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can respond to others using gestures or words while showing care for their feelings with support.
I can show respect when communicating with others with guidance.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.1.d|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.2|2.text: Recount or describe key ideas or details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.2|2.ee_text: Demonstrate an emerging understanding of a familiar text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media by answering questions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can fluently and comprehensively recount or describe the nuanced, complex key ideas and rich details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media, demonstrating a thorough understanding.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively recount or describe the key ideas and important details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can partially recount or describe some key ideas or details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media, but my recounts may be limited in scope or miss important information.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to recount or describe key ideas or details from texts read aloud or information presented orally/through other media. My recollections are often incomplete or inaccurate.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask and answer questions about key details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
I can pick from choices to answer questions about key details presented in a story read aloud (e.g., “What did Ruby want to do?”).
I can answer yes or no question about a story that was read aloud (e.g., I can indicates correct response when asked if Ruby went to school.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about key details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
I can answer yes or no questions about a key detail presented in a story read aloud after the teacher rereads the paragraph or page where the key detail is stated.
I can select the picture symbol from an array to answer a question about a video clip after the teacher stops the video on the key scene.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about a text read aloud or information presented through other media.
I can after listening to the story of Ruby Bridges and looking carefully at the pictures, point to a picture of Ruby when asked, “Where is Ruby?”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.2|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.3|2.text: Ask and answer questions about what a speaker says in order to gather additional information, or clarify something that is not understood, or expand on the topic.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.3|2.ee_text: Ask and answer questions about the details provided by the speaker, or expand on the topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I confidently and skillfully ask probing questions to deeply probe a speaker's message, gather comprehensive information, clarify complex points, and substantially expand the dialogue in insightful ways. My questioning and responding demonstrate a sophisticated understanding.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively ask and answer questions to gather additional relevant information, clarify anything that is not fully understood, and thoughtfully expand the discussion based on a speaker's message.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes ask and answer basic questions about what a speaker says, in order to get a bit more information, clarify minor points, or modestly expand the discussion. However, my questioning and responding skills are still developing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty asking and answering questions to gather more information, clarify understanding, or expand on a speaker's message. My questions and responses are often limited or ineffective.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can answer questions about what a speaker says.
I can Repeat the directions when a teacher asks, “What do you need to do next?”
I can Answer the question, “What do you want?” after the person working the lunch line states the options.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, answer questions about what a speaker says.
I can when the teacher asks, “What do you need to do next?” and given a choice of two of the steps, the student identifies the next step.
I can after the teacher assigns daily jobs to students (e.g., line leader, weather reporter, deliver attendance to the office), student identifies one of two or three symbols that represents his/her job for the day.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, respond when asked a question.
I can when asked, “What do you want?,” look at the objects being offered by the teacher.
I can when asked, “Where should we go?,” look at the door to the classroom.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.3|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.4|2.text: Tell a story or recount an experience with descriptivedetails, expressing ideas clearly.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.4|2.ee_text: Identify a photograph or object that reflects a personal experience and tell one detail about it.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I masterfully tell stories or recount experiences, incorporating vivid, carefully chosen descriptive details that allow me to express complex ideas and experiences in a clear, engaging, and sophisticated manner.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively tell stories or recount experiences, including descriptive details that help convey ideas clearly.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can partially tell stories or recount experiences, but my narratives may be lacking in descriptive details and clarity at times. I am still developing the ability to express my ideas clearly.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have difficulty telling stories or recounting experiences, even with support. My narratives lack descriptive details and clarity of expression.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify a photograph or object that reflects a personal experience and identify one detail about it.
I can use a photo to identify a trip to the water park and point out the slide in the picture.
I can Select a photo from a family trip to the park and tell about one thing that happened (e.g., “picnic,” “hotdogs”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify a photo or object that reflects a personal experience.
I can select a picture of a trip to the water park from a set of four photos when asked “Where did you go Saturday?”
I can Select a photo of self holding an art project and when asked “What did you make?”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify a photo or object of self engaged in an activity.
I can I can with guidance and support, eye gaze to a picture of a trip to the water park.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.4|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.5|2.text: Include digital media and visual displays in presentations to clarify or support ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.5|2.ee_text: Select visual, audio, or other digital media, and/or tactile representations to depict a personal experience.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I expertly integrate a variety of dynamic digital media and visual displays into my presentations, using them strategically and creatively to powerfully clarify, enhance, and support the clear, sophisticated expression of my complex ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I appropriately include digital media and visual displays in my presentations in order to clarify and support the expression of my ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes incorporate limited digital media or visual displays into my presentations, but the use of these supporting elements may not always effectively clarify or support my ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to include digital media or visual displays in my presentations. My presentations often lack the use of these supporting elements to clarify or enhance my ideas, thoughts, and feelings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a visual, audio, or tactual representation to depict an experience, thoughts, or feelings.
I can select from choices the pictures of the trip to the water park that depict the experience.
I can select a tactual material from a box of materials to represent how they feel about a new activity in P.E.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can select a picture or tactual representation to accompany a story.
I can after creating a predictable chart (I like <food>.) with the class during shared writing, select a picture to go with his page in the book (e.g., the student looks through a magazine to choose a picture).
I can during shared reading of a text, select a tactual material from a box of materials to represent the text on one page of the story.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a picture to accompany a story.
I can with guidance and support after creating a predictable chart (I like <food>.) with the class during shared writing, the student selects a picture to go with his page in the book from a small set of pictures provided by the teacher.
I can with guidance and support during shared reading of a text, student selects a tactual material from a box of materials to represent the text on one page of the story from a small set of tactuals provided by the teacher.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.2.5|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.a|2.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures and contexts; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening; and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. a. recognize and appreciate linguistic diversity (e.g., at home, in the community and in peer and professional writing and speaking).
WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.a|2.ee_text: use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. Notice linguistic diversity.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I exhibit a sophisticated, nuanced understanding of how language functions in diverse cultures and contexts. I deeply recognize, appreciate, and adeptly apply my knowledge of linguistic diversity to comprehend, compose, create, and speak with exceptional skill and sensitivity.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I demonstrate a solid understanding of how language functions in different cultures and contexts. I recognize and appreciate linguistic diversity in my reading, listening, composing, creating, and speaking.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I demonstrate a developing understanding of how language functions in different cultures and contexts. I sometimes recognize and appreciate linguistic diversity, but I do not consistently apply this knowledge effectively.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have a limited understanding of how language functions in different cultures and contexts. I rarely recognize or appreciate linguistic diversity in my reading, listening, composing, creating, or speaking.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can produce all letters.
I can use technology and tools to produce all letters.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can produce first letter in own name.
I can use writing tool to produce first letter of their name.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can explore letters and technology used to produce letters.

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.a|2.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain how people use different languages and ways of speaking at home, at school and in the community.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can recognize and appreciate linguistic diversity at home, in the community and in what I read and hear.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can name different languages people use in my school with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can notice that people speak in different ways with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can notice that people around me use different languages.

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.b|2.text: Recognize formal and informal uses of English.
WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.b|2.ee_text: Notice formal and informal uses of language.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I exhibit a sophisticated, nuanced understanding of formal and informal English usage. I effortlessly recognize and expertly navigate the appropriate application of language formality across a wide range of contexts and purposes.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can reliably recognize and distinguish between formal and informal uses of English. I apply this understanding appropriately in my reading, listening, composing, creating, and speaking.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I demonstrate a developing awareness of formal and informal uses of English, but I may not consistently recognize or apply this knowledge effectively in my own language use.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I have a limited ability to recognize the differences between formal and informal uses of English. I often confuse or misapply the appropriate level of language formality.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use frequently occurring nouns (e.g., mom, dad, boy, girl).
I can identify individuals using a frequently occurring noun such as mom, dad, boy, or girl, to the teacher using their routine mode of communication.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify symbols or objects that represent personally relevant, common nouns.
I can point to an object or person when named by an adult (e.g., Asked “Where is your coat?,” points to it.).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can interact with symbols or objects that represent personally relevant, common nouns.
I can when given coat and told, “Here is your coat,” reach for the coat.

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.b|2.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can switch between formal and informal English on purpose and explain why.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can recognize formal and informal uses of English.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can sort phrases into school talk and friend talk with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can tell whether someone is talking to a friend or a teacher with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can notice formal and informal uses of language.

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.1.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.a|2.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. a. Determine the meaning of a new word when a prefix or suffix is added.
WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.a|2.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. a. Demonstrate knowledge of new vocabulary drawn from reading and content areas.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I exhibit sophisticated skills in determining and clarifying the meanings of complex, ambiguous, or technical words and phrases. I expertly and flexibly apply a wide range of advanced strategies, demonstrating a nuanced understanding of how to derive meaning from language.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively determine and clarify the meanings of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in my reading and content. I reliably use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult references, and apply appropriate word solving strategies.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I demonstrate a developing ability to determine and clarify word and phrase meanings, sometimes using context clues, word parts, or other strategies, but my skills are still uneven.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I struggle to determine or clarify the meanings of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases. I have limited ability to use context clues, word parts, reference materials, or other strategies to figure out word meanings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use new words I learn from stories and texts.
I can show that I know the meanings of words from what I read and hear.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can learn and use new words from reading with help.
I can explain or point to what new words mean with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recognize or say a new word I learned from a story or lesson with help.
I can show or point to something that helps me understand new words with support.

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.a|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.b|2.text: Use a common root word as a clue to the meaning of an unknown word.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use root words to figure out the meaning of new words independently.
I can explain how the root word helps me understand the meaning of a more complex word.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use a common root word to help me understand the meaning of new words.
I can find root words in unfamiliar words to help me understand their meanings.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can recognize root words and use them to understand new words with some help.
I can try to use root words to figure out word meanings when guided.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize that some words have a root word, and with help, I can use it to understand the word’s meaning.
I can try to use a root word to help me understand a new word when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.b|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.c|2.text: Use individual words to predict meaning of compound words (e.g., birdhouse).

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can break down compound words and use the individual words to predict their meaning easily.
I can explain how the meaning of a compound word comes from its smaller parts.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use the meaning of individual words to figure out what a compound word like "birdhouse" means.
I can understand how two words combine to make the meaning of a compound word.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can break apart a compound word and try to use the smaller words to understand its meaning, with help.
I can try to guess the meaning of a compound word by looking at the individual words with guidance.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize a compound word and use the smaller words to help me understand its meaning when someone helps me.
I can try to use the words I know to understand the meaning of a compound word with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.c|2.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.d|2.text: Use resources to clarify the meanings of words.
WI-CC-ELA|L.2.2.d|2.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. d. Identify the words comprising compound words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I expertly and flexibly utilize a sophisticated repertoire of reference materials, both print and digital, to efficiently and effectively clarify the meanings of complex, nuanced, or technical vocabulary. I demonstrate an advanced ability to select and apply the most appropriate resource for the word learning task at hand.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I reliably use a variety of appropriate resources, such as dictionaries, glossaries, and thesauruses, to clarify the meanings of unknown words.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I sometimes use resources to clarify word meanings, but my use of reference materials may be limited or inconsistent in its effectiveness.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I rarely use resources to clarify the meanings of unknown words. I have difficulty identifying and accessing appropriate reference materials to support my word learning.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can break down compound words like "sunflower" into "sun" and "flower."
I can identify the two words that make up a compound word.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recognize and say the two words that make a compound word with some help.
I can point to or say the parts of a compound word with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:

I can adjust my reading rate and expression depending on the purpose and audience.

I can analyze and interpret complex texts, making connections to my own experiences and the world around me.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level texts accurately and fluently, even when they are challenging.
I can read aloud with appropriate pacing, expression, and volume, making the text come alive for the listener.
I can use context clues effectively to understand the meaning of unfamiliar words and complex sentences. I can also identify the main idea and supporting details of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read most grade-level texts with some accuracy, but I still make mistakes on longer or more difficult words.
I can read aloud with some fluency, but I may need to slow down or reread parts to make sure I understand them.
I can use context clues to figure out the meaning of most unfamiliar words, and I can usually understand the main idea of the text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can attempt to read grade-level text, but I often stumble over words and struggle to understand the meaning.
I can try to read aloud, but my reading is slow and choppy, and I don't always pay attention to punctuation or expression.
