I sometimes use context clues to guess at unfamiliar words, but I don't always understand the meaning of the text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can read familiar text with purpose and understanding.
I can when given a familiar text, read a selected passage. For example, when reading Ribsy, reads the passage, “Henry Huggins said . . . .”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can listen to familiar text with purpose and understanding.
I can when given a familiar text, listen to a familiar passage read aloud and answer comprehension questions.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen to familiar text.
I can when the teacher reads a familiar text, orient to the reader and attend to the task.
I can attend to a book on tape of a familiar text.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.a|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.b|3.text: read grade-level text orally with accuracy, appropriate rate, and expression on successive readings.
WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.b|3.ee_text: Use context to determine missing words that impede comprehension in familiar texts.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read grade-level text fluently and with expression, using appropriate pacing and tone to enhance the meaning and engage the audience.
I self-correct and adjust my reading in real-time to maintain accuracy and expression with minimal to no errors.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text with accuracy, making few errors and self-correcting when necessary.
I can read at an appropriate pace and use expression to reflect punctuation and meaning in the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read grade-level text with some accuracy, though I occasionally make mistakes and need support to correct them.
I can read at a mostly appropriate pace but sometimes need reminders to use expression and reflect the meaning of the text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With support, I can read parts of grade-level text with some accuracy, but I make frequent mistakes and need help to correct them.
I need assistance to read at an appropriate pace and to use expression when reading aloud.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use context clues with minimal support to determine missing words in familiar texts that affect my understanding.
I can identify when a missing word is causing confusion and seek help or reread to clarify meaning.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can sometimes use context clues to guess missing words with support from an adult, but I may not always recognize when comprehension is affected.
I need reminders to look back at the text and use clues to fill in gaps that impede my understanding.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
With significant support, I can use context clues to guess a few missing words in familiar texts, but I struggle to recognize when meaning is affected.
I can with support, identify gaps in the text and to use context clues to fill in missing information.

WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.b|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.c|3.text: use context to confirm or self- correct word recognition and understanding, rereading as necessary.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can independently use context to confirm or correct word recognition and understanding without the need for prompting.
I automatically reread parts of the text to ensure full comprehension and accuracy when encountering difficult words.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use context to confirm or self-correct word recognition and understanding with minimal support.
I recognize when rereading is necessary to help clarify meaning or correct a mistake.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use context to correct most words with some adult support, but I may need guidance to confirm understanding.
I may reread parts of the text when prompted by an adult to help correct or confirm word recognition.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can, with support, use context to recognize or correct a few familiar words, but I struggle to confirm understanding.
I need ongoing reminders and support to reread text for clarification or self-correction.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|RF.3.4.c|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.1|3.text: Develop and answer questions to locate relevant and specific details in a text to support an answer or inference. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.1|3.ee_text: Answer who and what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can ask and answer insightful questions about a text, using specific details and textual evidence to support my answer and make complex inferences.
I can analyze the text to identify the author's purpose and point of view.
I can use my understanding of the text to make connections to other texts and real-world experiences.
I can effectively communicate my understanding of the text through discussions and writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can ask and answer complex questions about a text, using specific details from the text to support my answer.
I can identify relevant details in the text and explain how they support my answer.
I can use evidence from the text to draw inferences and make predictions.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can ask and answer basic questions about a text, using some details from the text to support my answer.
I can identify some specific details in the text, but I may not always be able to use them effectively to support my answer.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can ask simple questions about a text, but I have difficulty identifying specific details to support my answer.
I may not understand the difference between a question and a statement.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can answer who and what questions to demonstrate understanding of details in a text.
I can use text evidence to support my answers.
I can identify the main idea of a text.
I can summarize the main events of a story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the main characters and setting in a story.
I can answer most who and what questions about the text.
I can use picture clues to help me answer questions about the text.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify the main characters in a story.
I can answer simple who and what questions about the text.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.1|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.2|3.text: Summarize portions of a text to determine a theme or central idea and explain how it is supported by key details. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can not only summarize portions of a text but also analyze how the author uses language and structure to develop the central idea or theme. I can connect the text to my own experiences and knowledge, and I can use my understanding of the text to draw conclusions and make predictions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can accurately summarize portions of a text, identifying the central idea or theme and supporting it with key details. My summaries are clear, concise, and organized.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify the main idea of a text and some key details that support it. My summaries are mostly accurate but may lack clarity or organization.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some key details from a text but struggle to connect them to a central idea or theme. My summaries are often incomplete or inaccurate.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify a detail of a text.
I can use guiding questions, identify a detail from a set of directions from choices (e.g., Directions for a “paper airplane.” Need “glue, paper.”).
I can use text supporting illustrations to identify a detail about the text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, identify a detail of a text.
I can use guiding questions to identify key details.
I can use highlighting tape to find key details.
I can use wax string, encircle or underline key words or details in a text (or in a set of picture directions, identify a step).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, match the topic of a text.
I can when given two pictures pick the one that is related to the text.
I can After reading the title and steps for a series of directions, repeat the title.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.2|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.3|3.text: Describe a character (traits, motivations, feelings) drawing on specific details from the text. (RL) Describe the relationship among a series of events, ideas, concepts, or steps in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.3|3.ee_text: Identify the feelings of characters in a story. (RL) Order two events from a text as “first” and “next. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author uses character traits and motivations to develop the plot of a story.
I can create a timeline or diagram to show the cause-and-effect relationships between events in a text.
I can use my understanding of character and event relationships to make predictions about what might happen next in a story or text.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can describe a character's traits, motivations, and feelings using specific details from the text.
I can describe the relationship between events, ideas, or concepts in a text, using language that pertains to time, sequence, and cause/effect.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can describe a character using a few details from the text.
I can explain how one event leads to another in a simple text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify some words that describe a character.
I can retell the order of events in a simple text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can list the progression of a series of events.
I can use a timeline, place events from an historical text in sequence.
I can use a graphic organizer, sequence events in a “First, Then, Then” progression.
I can After reading From Seed to Plant, sequence pictures in the correct order to show the growth of a seedling.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with prompting, list the progression of a series of events given the first event.
I can when given three directions to complete a task and the first direction, use sequence strips to order the remaining steps in the procedure correctly.
I can After repeated readings about Lewis and Clark’s expedition, place three pictures in sequence to represent progression of events on their expedition.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, determine sequence of events.
I can Shown the first step of a previously taught sequenced activity, indicate what comes next from illustrations on an activity sheet.
I can repeat a sequence of two directions in order.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.3|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.4|3.text: Determine the meaning of words, phrases, figurative language, and academic and content-specific words within a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.4|3.ee_text: Determine words and phrases that complete literal sentences in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use advanced vocabulary strategies, such as synonyms, antonyms, and etymology, to understand the meaning of complex words.
I can analyze the author's use of language to understand the tone, mood, and purpose of the text.
I can explain how word choice affects the meaning and impact of a text.
I can use my understanding of word meaning to make inferences and draw conclusions about the text.
I can apply my understanding of word meaning to real-life situations, such as understanding news articles, instructions, or complex conversations.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use context clues to determine the meaning of most unfamiliar words.
I can use a dictionary or glossary to look up the meaning of unfamiliar words and use them correctly in my own writing and speaking.
I can identify and explain the meaning of figurative language, such as similes, metaphors, personification, and hyperbole.
I can identify and explain the meaning of academic and content-specific words related to the text I am reading.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use context clues to guess the meaning of some unfamiliar words.
I can use a dictionary or glossary to look up the meaning of unfamiliar words.
I can identify the meaning of simple figurative language, such as similes and metaphors.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify familiar words in a text.
I can ask for help understanding unfamiliar words.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine the meaning of vocabulary related to a familiar text.
I can use visual tool (e.g., vocabulary graphic organizers) to help students to visualize the relationships between words and their possible meanings using pictures, definitions, or non-examples.
I can use an open-ended reading procedure to identify the correct word when choices are provided.
I can use a word bank to choose the meaning of a word in a familiar informational text.
I can use a picture dictionary to find the meaning of a word from a familiar text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify vocabulary in an informational text.
I can Match vocabulary words to the word in a text.
I can choose from an array of familiar words to complete sentences read aloud by an adult.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, locate identified vocabulary.
I can when given choices read by the teacher, match pictures to words.
I can Respond when hearing the correct word out of a choice of three words.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.4|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.5|3.text: Identify parts of stories, dramas, and poems using terms such as chapter, scene, and stanza. (RL) Identify and use text features to build comprehension. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.5|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support, determine the beginning, middle, and end of a familiar story with a logical order (RL) and use text features including headings and key words to locate information in a text (RI).

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can identify parts of texts beyond the basics, like flashbacks and foreshadowing.
I can analyze how authors use text features to create meaning.
I can use text features to make predictions about what will happen next in a text.
I can explain how text features can help me learn new information from different types of texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can identify all parts of stories, like chapters, scenes, and stanzas.
I can identify all text features, like titles, subtitles, captions, diagrams, and graphs.
I can use text features to help me understand what I am reading.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify most parts of stories, like chapters and scenes.
I can identify most text features, like titles, subtitles, and captions.
I can use some text features to help me understand what I am reading.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify some parts of stories, like the beginning and the end.
I can identify some text features, like pictures and headings.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine the beginning, middle, and end of a story.
I can use picture clues to identify an event that occurred in the beginning, middle, or end of the story.
I can use a story map, fill in the beginning and end of the story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify the beginning or ending of a story.
I can use picture clues to identify the beginning of a story.
I can when given a story map with the beginning and middle completed, identify the ending.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify one event from a story.
I can when given an array of pictures, choose one that matches something that happened in the story.
I can answering yes or no questions to respond, indicate whether an event was in the story.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.5|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.6|3.text: Discuss how the reader’s point of view or perspective may differ from that of the author, narrator, or characters in a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.6|3.ee_text: Identify personal point of view about a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how an author uses different techniques to convey different perspectives within a text.
I can discuss the impact of an author's perspective on the overall meaning of a text.
I can apply my understanding of different perspectives to real-life situations, such as understanding different viewpoints in a news article or recognizing bias in advertising.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can discuss how my own point of view differs from that of the author, narrator, or characters in a text.
I can explain how the author's point of view influences the way a story is told.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can explain how the main character's perspective changes throughout a story.
I can compare and contrast the perspectives of two different characters in a story.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify the main character in a story.
I can recognize that different characters in a story can have different opinions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify a personal point of view about a text.
I can when given three choices, select the choice that best represents their point of view about an assignment.
I can Point to the part or step on an activity sheet that they like best.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify personal point of view about the topic.
I can when given two choices, select the choice that best represents their own point of view about a topic (e.g., “Do you like ____ activity or do you like _____ activity best?”).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, express point of view about a topic.
I can Respond with gestures or facial expressions to topic.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.6|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.7|3.text: Explain how specific illustrations or text features contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a text (e.g., create mood, emphasize character or setting, or determine where, when, why, and how key events occur). (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.7|3.ee_text: Identify parts of illustrations or tactual information that depict story elements. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how specific illustrations or text features work together to create meaning in a text and explain how they enhance the reader's understanding of the text. I can also use this understanding to create my own texts that effectively use illustrations and text features to convey meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain how specific illustrations or text features contribute to what is conveyed by the words in a text, such as creating mood, emphasizing character or setting, or determining where, when, why, and how key events occur.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can identify specific illustrations or text features in a text and explain how they contribute to the meaning of a few words.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some illustrations or text features in a text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify parts of illustrations that depict a particular mood, setting, or character.
I can Find the part of the illustration that shows that the character is mad (e.g., the face, a fist, red face).
I can Find the part of the illustration that shows that the setting is gloomy (e.g., clouds, gray sky, no color).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use illustrations to describe characters and setting.
I can use an illustration from the text, generate words (character and setting), which are then put into sentences and are repeatedly accessed and used in the classroom (Calhoun’s Picture Word Inductive Model [PWIM]).
I can use an illustration of a character from the text, identify words from a list that describes how the character looks in the illustration.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify character or setting in an illustration from the text.
I can with guidance and support, identify the illustration that shows setting.
I can with guidance and support, identify the character from the text within an illustration.
I can Touch a picture of a character from the story, when given two illustrations, at least one of which is from the story.
I can Touch a picture of the setting of the story, when given two illustrations, at least one of which is from the story.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.7|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.8|3.text: Explain how claims in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.8|3.ee_text: Identify two related points the author makes in text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can clearly explain how multiple claims in a text are supported by relevant and strong reasons and evidence.
I can evaluate and compare the strength of evidence used to support claims in different sections of a text, and I can explain why certain reasons are more convincing than others.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can explain how the claims in a text are supported by relevant reasons and evidence.
I can identify specific pieces of evidence and directly link them to the claims they support.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify some claims in a text but need help to fully explain how they are supported by reasons and evidence.
I can find some evidence in a text but need guidance to connect it to the claims being made.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can find a claim in a text with support, but I need help identifying the reasons and evidence that support it.
I need adult assistance to understand the connection between claims and the evidence provided in a text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify two related points the author makes in a text with minimal support.
I can explain how the two points are connected or related to each other.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify one point the author makes in a text, and I need help to find the second point.
I can recognize that the points are related with some guidance, but I need help explaining how they are connected.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify one point the author makes in a text with significant support.
I need help understanding how the points in the text are related or connected to each other.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.8|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.9|3.text: ecognize genres and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.3.9|3.ee_text: Identify similarities between two texts and recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can analyze how authors use genre conventions to achieve specific effects.
I can make complex connections between a text and multiple other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations.
I can use my understanding of genre to create my own texts.
I can explain how genre shapes our understanding of the world around us.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can recognize a variety of genres, including fiction and nonfiction.
I can explain how different genres are used for different purposes.
I can make connections between a text and other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, personal events, and situations.
I can use evidence from the text to support my connections.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can identify different genres like biographies, news articles, and fairy tales.
I can explain how different genres use different features, like characters, plot, and setting.
I can make simple connections between a text and my own experiences.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can identify familiar genres like stories and poems.
I can notice some similarities between different texts I read.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can identify similarities and differences between two texts.
I can recognize that texts reflect one’s own and others’ culture.
I can explain how my own culture is similar to or different from other cultures.
I can use text evidence to support my answers.
I can discuss how cultural differences can enrich our lives.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can identify most similarities between two texts.
I can recognize how texts reflect different cultures.
I can explain how my own culture is similar to or different from other cultures.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify some similarities between two simple texts.
I can recognize that texts can be about different cultures.

WI-CC-ELA|R.3.9|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.1|3.text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.1|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can write complex and sophisticated essays and stories that engage the reader and convey my ideas effectively.
I can use my writing to persuade, inform, and entertain others.
I can use my writing to advocate for myself and others.
I can use my writing to make a difference in the world.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can compose reflective, formal, and creative writing for a variety of purposes, including high-stakes and low-stakes situations.
I can choose the appropriate writing style and format for each purpose.
I can use a variety of persuasive techniques and literary devices in my writing.
I can revise and edit my writing to improve its clarity, organization, and effectiveness.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can write longer paragraphs and short essays on a variety of topics.
I can use a variety of sentence structures and vocabulary words.
I can proofread my writing for errors in grammar, punctuation, and spelling.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can write simple sentences and short paragraphs on familiar topics.
I can use some basic punctuation and capitalization rules.
I can share my writing with others.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a text and write to state an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from the library, use a computer-based word bank to write It’s the best, and then refer to the book to find an example of what makes it the best and write about it.
I can select a text, write a word to express an opinion about it (e.g., lk [like]) and then, given a written frame with the word “because,” add a reason (e.g., fne [funny]).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select a text and write, draw, or dictate an opinion about it and one reason to support the opinion.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books and working with a teacher who guides the student to “write those words” and “type the sounds you hear in those words,” use a talking word processor and word prediction software to write good book and add one reason (e.g., lik barz [Like bears.]).
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, state an opinion (e.g., “bad’), attempt to write the word, and then have a teacher show how to use a word wall word (e.g., sad) to spell the word conventionally.
I can select a book from a collection of recently read books, then the teacher navigates through the student’s multiple message communication device to reveal messages that express an opinion, then selects a message communicating an opinion (e.g., “It’s really good!”) and when the teacher asks, “What makes it good?,” uses the device to answer (e.g., says “boy”) which the teacher interprets to mean the student liked the main character who was a boy and writes in chart form.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, state an opinion about a book.
I can look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite.” and then writes <Student’s name> likes <name of book> on the small group chart text.
I can in a small, teacher-led group, select 2-3 snack choices, write them down on a menu, and then select their snack later in the day from the menu.
I can Look at, touch, or take a book from a selection of two when the teacher asks, “Show me your favorite.”

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.1|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.a|3.text: write text in a variety of modes. a. Opinion pieces in which the student supports a point of view about a topic or text they are writing about, state an opinion, list reasons that support the opinion.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.a|3.ee_text: with guidance and support, use writing, dictation and/or drawing to compose: a. Opinion pieces in which they state an opinion about a topic or text and include at least one reason to support that opinion. b.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write well-developed opinion pieces that persuasively state my viewpoint and provide strong, logical reasons to support it. I can write informative texts that thoroughly explore a topic, incorporating a range of facts, definitions, details, and examples to effectively convey information.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an opinion piece that states an opinion and provides a list of reasons that support the opinion. I can write informative or explanatory texts that introduce a topic and use facts, definitions, and details to develop points.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an opinion piece that states my opinion and provides 1-2 reasons to support it. I can write an informative text that introduces a topic and includes some relevant facts, definitions, or details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a simple opinion piece with a basic statement of my opinion, but I struggle to provide reasons that support my view. I can write a basic informative text with a topic, but have difficulty including relevant facts, definitions, or details.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select a topic and write about it including one fact or detail.
I can select a topic by looking through a class photo album and then writes a label for one of the items in the photo.
I can select a topic from a book used during shared reading and then writes one fact from the book.
I can select a topic from a class chart of recent activities and then writes a remembered detail with an alternative keyboard (e.g., garden, dg dr <dig dirt>).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can write a fact or detail about a given topic.
I can when given an interactive whiteboard with a bank of words on a given topic, select words from the bank that are related to the topic to write a fact or detail about it.
I can select a fact or detail about a given topic from a list of facts and details.
I can when given a repeated line frame, contribute one detail to a group list about the topic (e.g., whales: Whales eat <fish>. Whales eat <krill>. Whales eat <plankton>.).
I can when read a short text by the teacher, suggest one idea to the class’s semantic web of details (e.g., pterodactyl: winged lizard, 40 feet long, flies, eats bugs, has four fingers), which the teacher writes and adds to the class dinosaur blog.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select a topic for use during shared writing.
I can when given a choice of three topics to use during shared writing, eye gaze, point, or touch one to indicate a choice which the group will then write about and read aloud for the student.
I can select the topic for a shared writing activity from two or more choices offered by the teacher, and then select a related picture on the topic to type about, from which the teacher will model a related fact (e.g., Child has a picture of a rock and types “ewfsatrhrgr” and the teacher says, “I like your writing. I could use that r (as she points) and write ‘rock.’ I see a rock.”).

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.a|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.b|3.text: Informative or explanatory texts in which they introduce a topic, use facts, definitions, and details to develop points.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.b|3.ee_text: Informative/Explanatory text in which they provide at least 2 facts about a predetermined or self chosen topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can introduce a topic clearly and develop it thoroughly using well-organized facts, definitions, and relevant details that enhance understanding.
I can use precise language and transitions to connect ideas, making my writing engaging and informative.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can introduce a topic and use facts, definitions, and details to develop and explain my points clearly.
I can organize my writing in a logical sequence that helps the reader understand my topic.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can introduce a topic and include some facts and definitions, but I need support to organize my details and develop my points fully.
I need help using clear transitions to connect ideas and make my writing flow smoothly.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With support, I can introduce a topic and include a few basic facts or definitions, but I struggle to develop points clearly.
I need significant guidance to organize my ideas and add enough details to make my writing informative.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can provide at least two facts about a predetermined or self-chosen topic that are accurate and relevant to the topic.
I can present my facts in a way that is understandable and related to the main idea of my writing.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can provide at least one fact about a predetermined or self-chosen topic with support, but I need help to find a second fact or make the connection to the topic clearer.
I need assistance organizing my facts, and my writing may need further development to explain the topic clearly.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with support, provide one fact about a predetermined or self-chosen topic, but I struggle to find a second fact or explain it clearly.
I need ongoing guidance to organize my ideas and ensure my facts are connected to the topic.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.b|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.c|3.text: Convey events, real or imagined, through narrative or short stories to develop experiences or events using descriptive details and clear event sequences to establish a situation and introduce a narrator or characters. use dialogue and description of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.c|3.ee_text: Convey events, real or imagined and narrate a single event or several loosely linked events. Include some details regarding what happened and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can craft engaging narrative stories that vividly convey experiences and events through the use of descriptive language, well-developed characters, and a clear, logical sequence of events. I can effectively use dialogue, character thoughts and actions to deeply explore how characters respond to different situations, showcasing a nuanced understanding of human nature.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can convey events, real or imagined, through narrative or short stories, using descriptive details and clear event sequences to establish a situation and introduce a narrator or characters. I can also use dialogue and description of actions, thoughts, and feelings to develop experiences and events or show the responses of characters to situations.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a story that has a clear sequence of events and includes some descriptive details, but my development of characters and their responses to situations is limited.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a simple story with some details, but I have difficulty establishing a sequence of events or developing characters through dialogue and description.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
descriptors.ee_emerging: I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience to write about in shared writing.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.2.c|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.a|3.text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Include an introduction that establishes a purpose and provides a concluding statement appropriate to the mode of writing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.a|3.ee_text: with guidance and support, use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that uses words familiar to the student, temporal words to signal event order, and a beginning, middle, and end.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can craft engaging, well-organized writing that hooks the reader with a compelling introduction, artfully uses a variety of transition words and phrases to guide the reader, and selects precise, vivid vocabulary that enhances the overall meaning and flow of my writing. I can effectively adapt my word choice and organizational structure to suit different purposes and audiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can create writing that has an introduction that establishes a purpose, uses transitions like "in addition", "for example", and "as a result" to link and build connections between ideas, and uses specific words to convey meaning and connect categories of information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write with an introduction and conclusion, and I try to use some transitions like "first", "then", and "in the end" to sequence my ideas. I use some general words to describe things.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write a few sentences with a beginning and an end, but I do not use any transitions or specific word choices to connect my ideas.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
I can choose to write about his own birthday and write, pte [party].
I can choose to write about going to visit grandparents and write, fn [fun].
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience and write one thing about it.
I can choose to write about their own birthday party and with support from the teacher who stretches out the word to isolate the sounds, write prte [party].
I can choose to write about the “fun” they had going to visit grandparents and with support from the teacher, who stretches out the word to isolate the sounds, write fan [fun].
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, select an event or personal experience to write about in shared writing.
I can choose by looking, pointing, or touching, an event from two choices presented by the teacher which the teacher then writes in the group’s shared text.
I can when given a teacher modeling the use of a multiple message voice output device and talking about the messages on the student’s My News page, select a message on a personal experience to use in shared writing (e.g., I went to my dad’s softball game. They won.), which the teacher will write down, reread aloud while pointing, and save.
I can express a reaction to a personal experience to be shared (e.g., After the teacher reviews free choice selections engaged in that day, she points to and labels each of the visual supports, and asks, “Did you like it?,” and the student responds [e.g., indicates yes by smiling], and the teacher writes, Brian liked art. Brian did not like the sand table. Brian liked his story. in his home-school journal, reading each aloud as she writes it, and the entire text while pointing after she finishes.).

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.a|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.b|3.text: Transitions: use prompts, words, and phrases to signal event order and to link and build connections between ideas, text, and events.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use a variety of transition words and phrases to connect ideas and events smoothly.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use words and phrases to show event order and link ideas, text and events.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use first, next and last to order events with a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use and or then to join ideas with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.b|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.c|3.text: Word Choice (including domain specific): use words familiar to the student for emphasis, addition, contrast, or order to connect categories or information, and to convey meaning.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose exact words to add emphasis, contrast or order and explain my choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use familiar words to add emphasis, addition, contrast or order and connect my ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use also, but or then from a word bank to connect ideas.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a few topic words to tell about a picture with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not Applicable

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.3.c|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.4|3.text: ith support from adults and peers, produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task and purpose. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.4|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate for an explicitly stated task, and expresses more than one idea.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently produce well-developed, culturally-relevant writing that clearly communicates my purpose and engages my audience in a meaningful way.
descriptors.cc_at_target: With support from adults and peers, I can produce writing in which the development and organization are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to the task and purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: With support, I can write in a way that starts to show cultural awareness and a sense of purpose, but my organization and development still need improvement.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write with support, but my writing does not yet reflect cultural awareness or a clear purpose.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that expresses more than one idea.
I can when working with peers, write one fact about a group project, talk with peers about the fact, and add one more fact with peer support.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers, contribute to a shared writing about a shared reading that includes at least two ideas related to a selected topic.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that expresses an idea.
I can use a preprogrammed computer set-up with full alphabet access to write one idea.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers, contribute a written idea to a shared writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, express an idea.
I can when working with the teacher and a group of peers on a shared writing project, select from an array of choices to express an idea.
I can use a preprogrammed single message voice output device, express an idea to include in a writing project.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.4|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.5|3.text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, respond to questions and suggestions from peers and add details to strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, and editing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.5|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, including questions or suggestions, revise their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently respond to feedback, plan, revise, and edit my writing to effectively strengthen it, and I can provide constructive feedback to my peers to help them improve their writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can respond to questions and suggestions from peers, and with guidance and support, I can plan, revise, and edit my writing to add details and strengthen it.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write with some guidance and try to respond to feedback, but I have difficulty planning, revising, or editing my work to strengthen it.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can try to write with some help, but I have trouble responding to feedback or making changes to improve my writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, revise own writing by adding more information.
I can select writing from own writing folder, share it with peers, and then revise it by adding more information based on the ideas provided by peers.
I can share writing with the teacher using a talking word processor to read it out loud, listen to the teacher talk about the writing, and then add more information based on what the teacher says.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more to own writing.
I can when working with a small group of peers to write a thank you note to a parent who helped the class, write one word and add another when a peer says, “Tell them why you’re thanking them,” or “tell them more about why you liked them helping.”
I can write using a talking word processor, read it back to the group using the software, and then add more when suggestions are offered by peers.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing.
I can when working on a tablet computer with an onscreen keyboard that speaks the letter names, select letters to produce writing.
I can use two-switch partner-assisted scanning, direct an adult to point to/say the next letter of the alphabet and indicate, “write that one down.” when the teacher points to/says a desired letter.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.5|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.6|3.text: ith guidance and support from adults and peers, use digital tools to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with peers. Learn to produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.6|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support from adults, use digital tools to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Learn to produce writing through printing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently use a variety of digital tools to produce and publish high-quality, multi-paragraph writing, collaborating effectively with my peers. I can fluently produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing, and I use these skills to communicate my ideas in real-world situations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use digital tools with guidance and support from adults and peers to produce and publish writing, including in collaboration with others. I can also produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use digital tools with some guidance from adults or peers to produce and publish simple, short pieces of writing.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use digital tools with a lot of help from adults or peers, but I still struggle to produce and publish any writing.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce writing while interacting and collaborating with others.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use a single switch to scan through choices in an onscreen word bank and peers expand on the word in a collaborative writing project.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use an alternative keyboard while a peer uses a standard keyboard for the pair to work together in producing a collaborative writing project.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use assistive technology to post a comment in response to a text posted on an Internet site (e.g., a children’s reading site, a class science blog, or a children’s author’s homepage).
I can with guidance and support, use assistive technology to engage in instant messaging with another student or volunteer in a digital communication environment (e.g., a cellphone, an online communication site).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce writing.
I can when working with the teacher, use a switch to scan through choices in an onscreen word bank and select words to produce writing.
I can when working with the classroom aide, use spelling prediction and voice output to compose simple texts for inclusion in a class anthology.
I can when working with an adult and word prediction software, select a letter on the keyboard, scan through the choices that are produced by the word prediction software, and select a word to produce writing.
I can with guidance and support from adults, use a single switch to scan through choices in an onscreen word bank and peers expand on the word(s) in a collaborative writing project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults, use technology to produce written communications.
I can with guidance and support from an adult, use a multiple message voice output device to make a choice, which is then written down, read aloud to the student, and acted upon.
I can with guidance and support from an adult, use an app on a tablet device to make a comment, which is saved and/or printed.
I can take turns selecting preprogrammed messages from an alternative keyboard, listen as the message is read/typed by a talking word processing program, and then observe as others act on the message (e.g., “May I please have another book to read?” “Could I please go to the writing center now?” “Is it time for recess?”).

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.6|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.7|3.text: Conduct short inquiry projectsthat build knowledge about a topic.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.7|3.ee_text: EE..W.3.7 . with guidance and support, identify information about a shared or independent inquiry topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently conduct thorough inquiry projects that allow me to develop in-depth knowledge about a topic, and I can effectively present my findings to others.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct short inquiry projects that build my knowledge about a topic.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can conduct a short inquiry project and gather some information about a topic, but I may still struggle to stay on task or identify the most relevant details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can start to explore a topic but have trouble staying focused or gathering relevant information.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can gather information about a topic from one source for a group research project.
I can when given a text displayed on an interactive whiteboard, select one piece of information to include in a group research activity.
I can when given screen reading software that reads the text on a webpage, select information to include in a group research project.
I can with guidance and support, locate information, then copy and paste it from a digital document into the group’s digital writing software.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, gather information about a topic from one source for a group research project.
I can when given a text displayed on an interactive whiteboard, work with a peer to identify one piece of information to include in a group research project.
I can when given screen reading software that reads the text on a webpage, work with peers to identify information to include in a group research project.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, explore one information source while writing.
I can use a single switch to advance through the pages of a digitized text, while using assistive technology.
I can explore a webpage with a screen reader on a tablet device, then use assistive technology to type letters while looking at a picture from the webpage.
I can while looking through a digital presentation of pictures related to a group’s research project, choose letters and words to accompany a picture, which will be added to the project.
I can select a digital picture for a classmate to add to the project and write about, always reading aloud the resulting product to Emerging Students.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.7|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.8|3.text: Recall information from experiences or gather information from print and digital sources; take brief notes on sources and sort evidence into provided categories.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.8|3.ee_text: Sort information on a topic or personal experience into two provided categories and write or draw about each one.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can easily recall relevant information from my experiences and efficiently gather information from a variety of print and digital sources. I can take thorough notes and skillfully sort the evidence into appropriate, self-created categories to support my learning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recall information from my experiences and gather information from print and digital sources. I can take brief notes on the sources and sort the evidence into provided categories.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recall some information from my own experiences and gather a little information from print and digital sources. I can take some brief notes, but have trouble sorting the evidence into categories
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sometimes recall information from my own experiences, but I have trouble gathering information from sources or taking notes.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can sort information into two provided categories and write information learned about them.
I can with guidance and support, given a list of adjectives that describe people, sort them into words that are nice and not nice, then write a summary statement about one or both categories (e.g., Nice people help. Mean people hurt you.).
I can with guidance and support, list tools and clothing used when planting in the class garden, and then make a statement about the use of each (e.g., Clothing helps skin. Tools dig dirt.)
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, sort information into provided categories and label the categories.
I can when working with the teacher who identifies the categories each time, the student selects another piece of information and places each piece of information into the appropriate category.
I can when working with a small group, sort adjectives that describe people, and then name the categories (e.g., nice/not nice, friendly/mean), and write a group repeated line text (e.g., Nice people help. Nice people smile. Nice people say please.).
I can with guidance and support of an adult, given pictures or words displayed on an interactive whiteboard, drag them into two boxes, label the categories, and write a statement about what is known about the categories (e.g., drag rake, shovel, and hoe into a category and name it tools and then write as a group, “Tools help you work.”).
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify information related to a given topic and write about it.
I can with guidance and support, indicate information about a given topic (e.g., during lunch, the teacher holds up the milk carton and half of a sandwich and asks the student to “Show me the drink,” and the student eye gazes, points to, or touches the milk, and the teacher adds to a nearby drink/eat chart, “Sam drinks milk.”).
I can with guidance and support, indicate words and pictures related to a given topic (e.g., when given a topic of favorite foods, add relevant pictures, and then using a word bank to choose and print “Yummy.”).

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.8|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.9|3.text: Recall facts from literary or informational texts to support reflection and inquiry.
WI-CC-ELA|W.3.9|3.ee_text: ith guidance and support from adults, recall key details from literary or informational texts and generate reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can thoroughly recall and analyze relevant facts from texts, using them to develop insightful reflections and meaningful questions that demonstrate a deep understanding of the subject matter.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recall important facts from literary or informational texts and use them to support my own reflection and inquiry.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can recall some key facts from a text and begin to use them to support my own thoughts and questions, but I have difficulty making clear connections.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can recall a few simple facts from a text, but I struggle to use them to support my own thoughts or questions.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can with guidance and support from adults, I can recall key details from literary or informational texts and generate reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.
I can use text evidence to support my answers and questions.
I can ask questions that demonstrate my understanding of the text.
I can ask questions that explore different perspectives on the text.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can recall most key details from a text with some support from an adult.
I can ask more complex questions about a text with some support from an adult.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can recall some key details from a text with support from an adult.
I can ask simple questions about a text with support from an adult.

WI-CC-ELA|W.3.9|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.a|3.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher led) with diverse partners on topics and texts, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. a. Come to discussions prepared, explicitly draw on topics and texts along with personal knowledge and experiences to explore ideas under discussion.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.a|3.ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. a. Engage in collaborative interactions about texts, pulling from prior experiences.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can lead a collaborative discussion, guiding the group to explore ideas in depth. I actively listen, ask thoughtful questions, and skillfully connect my ideas to those of others. I can synthesize information and present my own well-reasoned conclusions.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can effectively engage in a range of collaborative discussions. I come prepared, using the topic, text, and my own experiences to explore ideas. I follow agreed-upon discussion norms, ask relevant questions, and clearly explain my own understanding.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can join in a discussion, but I struggle to stay focused and on topic. I sometimes ask questions to understand the information, but I have a hard time clearly explaining my own thoughts.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sometimes join in a discussion, but I often interrupt others and do not listen carefully. I have difficulty connecting my own ideas to the discussion topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can engage in collaborative interactions about texts.
I can sign, “fox ate man” to build upon a peer’s response when the teacher asks the small group, “What happened to the gingerbread man at the end of the story?” and a peer replies, “he ate him.”
I can after hearing the story of The Gingerbread Man, contribute words that describe the gingerbread man to the list being generated by peers.
I can after a shared reading of a fable in a small group taking turns talking about the fable with the teacher’s involvement.
I can in a cooperative group, tell how the story is like his/her life.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can engage in multiple-turn exchanges with peers.
I can during lunchtime, communicate about the weekend by taking multiple turns with peers and adults who are sitting at the table.
I can Work with a peer to identify the animals that were in the gingerbread man story by eye gazing to pictures of the animals while the peer writes a list.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate an idea to the teacher or peer.
I can focus on the picture of the gingerbread man in the book, when asked who the story was about.
I can select the message more from multiple-location communication devices when the teacher says, “We’re all done for now.”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.a|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.b|3.text: Follow agreed-upon norms for discussions (e.g., gaining attention in respectful ways, actively listening, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.b|3.ee_text: b. Listen to others’ ideas before responding.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can consistently follow discussion norms, actively listen, and make thoughtful contributions that move the conversation forward. I can also help guide the discussion by redirecting it when needed and encouraging quieter participants to share their ideas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can follow agreed-upon norms for discussions, such as gaining attention in respectful ways, actively listening, and speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can mostly follow discussion norms like waiting for my turn to speak, but I still have difficulty actively listening and contributing meaningfully to the conversation.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sometimes follow basic discussion rules like raising my hand, but I often interrupt others and have trouble staying focused on the topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can listen to others’ ideas before responding.
I can Respond appropriately to indicate agreement or disagreement with the comments of others.
I can answer questions about what a peer has offered in a discussion.
I can Add a comment following a peer’s statement that indicates they have listened to the peer’s idea.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, listen to others’ ideas before responding.
I can wait for a peer to finish talking when an adult says, “Let Sally finish,” and then nods or signs to indicate agreement with the peer’s idea.
I can wait to provide a word that describes the gingerbread man when the teacher says, “One at a time. John is going first.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, add to or support others’ ideas.
I can with guidance and support, respond yes or no after the teacher says, “John said the gingerbread man was brave. Do you think he was brave?”
I can after interrupting when a peer or teacher is talking (e.g., vocalizing, speaking, activating communication device), student quiets when teacher reminds him or her to “Wait until Jose has finished.”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.b|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.c|3.text: Ask questions to check understanding of information presented, stay on topic, and link their comments to the remarks of others.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.c|3.ee_text: c. Indicate confusion or lack of understanding about information presented.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence from the discussion to support my ideas. I can explain how my thinking has changed or evolved as a result of the discussion. I can connect my ideas to the ideas of others in the discussion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain my own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion. I can use examples from the discussion to support my thinking.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain my ideas, but I may not connect them to the discussion.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share my thoughts and ideas about a topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask questions that link to ideas of others.
I can After listening to the book, Ramona Quimby, Age 8, a peer says, “I like her,” the student asks, “Who?”
I can After a peer offers an idea about what happened in a story or activity, asks, “What about . . . ?”
descriptors.ee_approaching: I can with guidance and support, ask questions that link to ideas of others.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, ask questions of others.
I can use a single message voice output device to ask, “What?” during a small group discussion after shared reading of a book.
I can select from three question words (what, where, when) on a voice output device to ask questions of peers during a literature circle.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.c|3.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can ask questions that check understanding and connect my comments to several classmates' ideas.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can ask questions to check understanding, stay on topic and link my comments to what others say.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can ask one question about the topic using a question starter.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can stay on topic and say one thing about it with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can show when I am confused or do not understand information.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.c|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.d|3.text: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use evidence from the discussion to support my ideas. I can explain how my thinking has changed or evolved as a result of the discussion. I can connect my ideas to the ideas of others in the discussion.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can explain my ideas, but I may not connect them to the discussion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can share my thoughts and ideas about a topic.
descriptors.cc_emerging: Explain their own ideas and understanding in light of the discussion.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can express ideas clearly.
I can when the teacher asks what Ramona did with the egg, use a voice output device to combine words and say, “head break.”
I can during the morning meeting, when the teacher asks, “How should we decorate our bulletin board today?,” reply, “blue, planets, stars.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, express ideas.
I can when the teacher shows two illustrations from the book and describes each, point to their favorite when asked, “Show me your favorite.”
I can during the morning meeting, when the teacher shows students three colors of construction paper and says, “We are going to decorate our bulletin board for our unit on the planets. What color should we make the background?,” eye gazes to black.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can communicate an idea to teacher or peer.
I can focus on the picture of the gingerbread man in the book, when asked who the story was about.
I can select the message more from a multiple-location communication device when the teacher says, “We’re all done for now.”

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.1.d|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.2|3.text: Determine main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diversemedia and formats.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.2|3.ee_text: Identify details in a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how main ideas and supporting details work together to create a clear and coherent message. I can explain how different types of media and formats can be used to present information effectively. I can use my understanding of main ideas and supporting details to summarize and synthesize information from a variety of sources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine main ideas and supporting details of a text read aloud or information presented in diverse media and formats.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes identify the main idea of a story or text, but I may have trouble finding supporting details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some basic facts from a story or text.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask and answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
I can pick from choices to answer questions about key details presented in a story read aloud (“What did Ruby want to do?”) and follow by asking a question.
I can answer yes or no question about a story that was read aloud (e.g., indicates correct response when asked if Ruby went to school) and follow with question, “Why she go?”
I can ask a question about information that is shared about the schedule (“Can we go outside?”) and respond to the teacher’s question that follows (“What do you want to play?”).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or through other media.
I can answer yes or no questions about a key detail presented in a story read aloud (e.g., indicates “no” when asked if Ruby was in the story).
I can select the picture symbol from an array to answer a question about a video clip the teacher shared with the class.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can maintain attention to the screen during a short video presentation.
I can respond when asked, “Do you like this?” to indicate attention during a teacher-conducted demonstration.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.2|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.3|3.text: Ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering elaboration and detail.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.3|3.ee_text: Ask or answer questions about the details provided by the speaker.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask thoughtful and insightful questions that demonstrate my understanding of the speaker's message. I can provide detailed and informative answers that go beyond simple recall. I can use my understanding of the speaker's message to make connections to other information or experiences.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can ask and answer questions about information from a speaker, offering elaboration and detail.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can answer questions about a speaker's message, but my answers may be brief or incomplete.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can ask simple questions about a speaker's message.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can ask or answer a question about what a speaker says.
I can After listening to the teacher give directions about a class activity, answer the question, “What do we do first?” by pointing to the station where they should start.
I can After listening to the teacher give directions about a class activity, ask a question using a multiple message voice output device combining the words, “Who with me?”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can answer questions about what a speaker says.
I can repeat the directions when a teacher asks, “What do you need to do next?”
I can 
I can with guidance and support, after listening to directions for an activity, look at the center where the activity will begin when asked, “Where do you go now?”
I can with guidance and support after listening to an adult read the options for lunch, eye gaze to the photograph of desired meal.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.3|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.4|3.text: Report on a topic or text, tell a story, read a poem, or recount an experience with facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.4|3.ee_text: Recount a personal experience, story, poem, or topic including details.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create engaging and informative presentations that include a variety of details and sensory language. I can use my voice to convey emotion and emphasis. I can adapt my speaking style to different audiences and situations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can report on a topic or text, tell a story, read a poem, or recount an experience with facts and relevant, descriptive details, speaking clearly at an understandable pace.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell a simple story or recount an experience, but I may leave out important details.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share a few basic facts about a topic or story.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can recount a personal experience including details.
I can use a multiple message voice output device, select three pictures to show how he or she made the cookie.
I can use a multiple voice output communication device to report on weekend activities during a morning meeting, saying, “Shopping with mom. Shoes, DVD, lunch.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use pictures or other visual or tactual supports to recount a personal experience including details.
I can use the class’ recipe (with printed steps, accompanied by pictures) to recount the steps to making cookies including details (e.g., “I put frosting on cookie - eyes and mouth. I ate him!”).
I can look at a photo of the class at the museum and uses multiple message voice output device to say, “Friends went bus. Saw dinosaurs.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, communicate a personal experience.
I can during the morning meeting, select a single message on My News page in communication system that has been programmed to say, “We went shopping this weekend. I got new shoes. Check them out! Aren’t they cool?” (Note: Student selects a single button on communication device to say this whole message.)
I can during snack time, tell group, “I make cookies.”
I can when given two options verbally of how to eat a gingerbread man, repeat the one they prefer.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.4|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.5|3.text: Include digital media and visual displays in presentations to enhance certain facts and details.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.5|3.ee_text: Create a multimedia presentation of a story or poem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can strategically select and use digital media and visual displays to engage my audience and effectively communicate my message. I can explain how different types of media can enhance different aspects of a presentation. I can use technology to create dynamic and interactive presentations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can include digital media and visual displays in presentations to enhance certain facts and details.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use simple visual aids, like pictures or drawings, in my presentations.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share information verbally in a presentation.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can create a multimedia presentation of a story or poem.
I can select images and add sound effects, music, and/or recording to go with a favorite poem.
I can Sequence the pages of a favorite story to put them in order in a multimedia version of the book.
I can record the cookie-making story and play it for the class, hitting switch to display several pictures to go with the story.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can participate in the creation of a multimedia presentation of a story or poem by adding words, selecting visuals, or recording portions of the text.
I can use a single message voice output device to record the repetitive phrase to play at appropriate times in the story (e.g., “Run, run, as fast as you can . . . .”).
I can select the images to accompany a text typed and recorded by partners in a group.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, participate in the creation of a multimedia presentation of a story or poem by adding words, selecting visuals, or recording portions of the text.
I can with cueing from peers, use a single message voice output device with the repetitive phrase recorded to play at appropriate times in the story (“Run, run, as fast as you can . . . .”).
I can when given a choice of two good photos selected by peers to accompany a page in a PowerPoint presentation of a story, use eye gazes to select the one they will use.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.3.5|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.3.1.a|3.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. a. Compare and contrast the ways in which language is used in familiar contexts (e.g., at home, in the community, in peer and professional writing/speaking).
WI-CC-ELA|L.3.1.a|3.ee_text: use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. use language to make simple requests, comment, or share information.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how language is used in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines. I can use my understanding of language to communicate effectively in a variety of situations. I can adapt my language to different audiences and purposes. I can explain how the conventions of written and spoken English differ and use this knowledge to improve my writing and speaking.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some basic differences in how people talk at home versus at school.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use noun + verb, noun + adjective, and subject + verb + object combinations in communication.
I can respond, “I like it” when asked for an opinion.
I can comment, “You nice.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can use noun + verb combinations when communicating.
I can say noun and verb “ball roll.”
I can signal or use communication device to say, “drink juice.”
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, identify common nouns and verbs in symbolic form.
I can point to symbols provided by the teacher to identify activity (e.g., when asked, “What do you want to do?” and provided with symbols for possible choices, the student points to the symbol for “drink.”

WI-CC-ELA|L.3.1.a|3.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.3.1.b|3.text: Recognize differences between the conventions of written and spoken English.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how key words and phrases contribute to the overall meaning and impact of a text. I can use my understanding of word choice to create vivid and engaging writing and speaking. I can explain how different word choices can affect the tone and meaning of a text. I can use my knowledge of word choice to improve my communication skills in a variety of situations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify key words and phrases that help readers understand a topic. I can choose words and phrases for effect when writing and speaking.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sometimes point out words or phrases that seem important in a story or text.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can identify some basic words in a story or text.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.3.1.b|3.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can explain several differences between written and spoken English and choose the right one for my purpose.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can recognize differences between the conventions of written and spoken English.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can tell one difference between how I talk and how I write with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a sentence is spoken or written with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: Not applicable
