Ex: A student understands that words like "but" and "so" can connect ideas in a sentence but may sometimes use them incorrectly or rely on a limited set of transitions.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can sometimes identify simple signal words like "and" and "but" in stories and use them in my writing. I can use some basic vocabulary words when I write and speak.
Ex: A student, when writing a story, uses words like "and," "but," and "because" to connect simple sentences.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use new formal/academic words that I learn from talking with others, listening to stories, and reading together with my class. I can use these words, even special words related to what we are learning about, in my own writing and speaking. I can also identify conjunctions (words like "and," "but," "or") in sentences.
Ex: After a lesson on weather, a student uses words like "precipitation," "temperature," and "forecast" in a conversation about the day's weather.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can understand and use new words that I hear when people talk and when I am read to. I can sometimes use these words to talk about what I am learning in different subjects.
Ex: A student, after listening to a story about a farm, correctly uses words like "tractor" and "harvest" in a sentence.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can understand and use new basic words that I hear often in different places.
Ex: A student learns and uses a new word like "vehicle" after it is introduced and reinforced in various contexts (e.g., books, classroom discussions, real-life observations).

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.4.a|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.a|5.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: a. conjunctions,
WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.a|5.ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use frequently occurring conjunctions: and, but, or, for, because.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use a variety of grammar and punctuation rules in my writing and speaking to create specific effects and make my writing more interesting. I can change how I use language depending on who I am talking or writing to and what the situation is. I can also explain how different grammar choices can change the meaning of what I am saying. I can even use my knowledge of grammar to analyze and critique the writing and speaking of others.
Ex: A student might explain how using the subjunctive mood ("If I were...") creates a hypothetical scenario compared to the indicative mood ("If I am...").
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use the rules of grammar and punctuation correctly in my writing and speaking. I understand why it is important to use standardized English in certain situations, like formal writing or presentations. I can use a variety of conjunctions, verb tenses, correlative conjunctions, and "they" and "their" to refer to singular people or ideas to make my writing clearer and more interesting. I can also find and fix grammar and punctuation mistakes in my own writing.
Ex: A student can use correlative conjunctions like "not only...but also" to connect ideas in a sentence and demonstrate an understanding of their function.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can sometimes use most grammar and punctuation rules correctly in my writing and speaking. I understand when it is appropriate to use standardized English. I can use a variety of conjunctions and verb tenses to express different meanings in my writing. I am learning how to use correlative conjunctions and "they" and "their" to refer to singular people or ideas.
Ex: A student understands that the past perfect tense ("had walked") shows an action completed before another past action but may still make occasional errors in its application.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With support, I can sometimes use basic grammar and punctuation rules in my writing and speaking. I can identify some situations where using standardized English is important. I can use some conjunctions and verb tenses, but I am still learning how to choose the right ones for different situations. I am not yet familiar with correlative conjunctions or using "they" and "their" to refer to singular people or ideas.
Ex: A student can consistently use simple conjunctions like "and" and "but" to combine sentences but may struggle with more complex conjunctions like "although" or "however."
descriptors.ee_at_target:
With support, I can sometimes use the correct grammar and word forms when I am talking and writing. I can use conjunctions like "and," "but," "or," "for," and "because" to connect my ideas. I can also use the past tense of common irregular verbs, like "went," "sat," "ate," and "told," correctly.
Ex: A student, when recounting a past event, accurately uses verbs like "went" and "saw" instead of "goed" and "seed."
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I am learning to use the correct grammar when I am talking and writing. I can use simple conjunctions like "and" and "but" to connect my ideas. I am learning to use the past tense of common verbs.
Ex: A student uses "and" to connect two ideas in a sentence but may need prompting to use other conjunctions like "because" to express a reason.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I am learning to use words to tell you what I am thinking. I am learning to use words like "and" to connect my ideas. I am learning about action words.
Ex: A student, when describing a picture, can use simple sentences like "The boy went to the park" with appropriate verb tense.

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.a|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.b|5.text: Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with verb tenses
WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.b|5.ee_text: Form and use the past tense of frequently occurring irregularverbs (e.g., went, sat, ate, told)

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use and explain verb tenses like past, present, and future to show when things happen (e.g., "I used 'will go' for future tense to show something that hasn't happened yet").
I can choose the correct verb tense to make my writing clearer and more accurate.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use verb tenses correctly in my writing to show when something happened (e.g., "I used 'played' to show it already happened").
I can explain the difference between past, present, and future tenses.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use verb tenses with some help in my writing (e.g., "With help, I wrote 'went' to show something happened in the past").
I can try to explain the difference between tenses with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can try to use simple verb tenses like past or present in my writing with help (e.g., "With help, I wrote 'go' to show something happening now").
I can try to explain how verb tenses work when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use past tense verbs like “went,” “ate,” or “sat” to talk about something that happened.
I can tell a story using the correct past tense of common verbs, like “told” or “saw.”
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can say or write past tense verbs like “went” or “ate” with help.
I can use past tense verbs when talking about something that happened with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen to a sentence about the past and repeat the correct verb, like “sat” or “went,” with support.
I can recognize and use one action that happened in the past with help.

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.b|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.c|5.text: Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with correlative conjunctions.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use correlative conjunctions like "either...or" and "neither...nor" in my writing to link ideas and explain their use (e.g., "I used 'either...or' to show two possible choices").
I can easily identify and correct errors when using correlative conjunctions in my writing.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use correlative conjunctions in sentences (e.g., "I used 'both...and' to connect two ideas in my sentence").
I can explain how correlative conjunctions help join related ideas in writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use correlative conjunctions like "either...or" with some help (e.g., "With help, I wrote 'either' and 'or' to show a choice between two things").
I can try to explain how these conjunctions connect ideas with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize correlative conjunctions like "both...and" and try to use them with help (e.g., "With help, I used 'both' and 'and' in my sentence").
I can try to understand how these words work when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.c|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.d|5.text: Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with use of “they” and “their” when referring to singular people or ideas.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can correctly use "they" and "their" to refer to a singular person in my writing (e.g., "I wrote 'They went to the store' to refer to one person").
I can explain how "they" and "their" are used to refer to singular people without confusing the reader.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use "they" and "their" correctly to refer to a singular person (e.g., "I used 'they' to refer to one student in my sentence").
I can explain how to use these words in a sentence to avoid confusion.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use "they" and "their" with help when referring to a single person (e.g., "With help, I wrote 'They went to the store' to talk about one person").
I can try to explain how these words are used with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can recognize when to use "they" and "their" to refer to a single person with help (e.g., "With help, I used 'their' to talk about someone's book").
I can try to understand how to use these words in a sentence when someone helps me.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.5.d|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.a|5.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: a. commas (introductory elements, and elements that need to be set off like a question or direct address);
WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.a|5.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can use a variety of punctuation marks and capitalization rules to make my writing more interesting and clear. I can change how I use these conventions depending on what I am writing and who will read it. I can explain why I chose to use certain conventions in my writing. I can use my knowledge of conventions to edit and improve my writing so that it is clear, correct, and interesting to read. I can also use these conventions correctly in real-life writing, like emails, letters, and reports.
Ex: A student might choose to use a semicolon to connect two closely related independent clauses for a more sophisticated effect than using a conjunction.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can use capital letters, punctuation marks, and correct spelling in my writing. I understand how to use commas, italics, underlining, and quotation marks for different purposes. I can use these conventions in my writing to make it easier to understand. I can also find and fix mistakes in my own writing and in the writing of others.
Ex: A student correctly uses commas after introductory phrases like "After school," or "In the morning," demonstrating an understanding of their function.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can use capital letters at the beginning of sentences and for proper nouns. I can use periods and commas in my writing, and I know when to use them in simple sentences. I can spell most words that students my age are expected to know, but I still make some spelling mistakes.
Ex: A student understands the basic use of quotation marks for dialogue but may occasionally forget to close quotation marks or use them incorrectly for emphasis.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
With some support, I remember to use capital letters at the beginning of sentences and for names of people and places. I am learning to use periods and commas in my writing. I can spell some simple words correctly, but I am still learning how to spell longer or more difficult words.
Ex: A student can consistently capitalize the first letter of a sentence and use a period at the end, indicating progress towards mastering basic punctuation.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I am learning to use the correct spelling, punctuation, and capitalization when I am writing. I can sound out words I don't know using what I know about letters and sounds and spelling patterns to try to spell them correctly.
Ex: A student attempts to spell "community" as "komunitee," demonstrating an understanding of phonetic spelling and common letter combinations.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I am learning to use what I know about letters and sounds to spell words.
Ex: A student, when asked to write "rain," can segment the sounds and write "ran" or "rane," showing progress in applying phonics knowledge.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify different letters of the alphabet. I am learning the sounds that letters make.
Ex: A student can identify the letters in their name and attempt to write some of them, demonstrating early literacy development.

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.a|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.b|5.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: b. italics, underlining, quotes with titles; and

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read grade-level text with accuracy and fluency, understanding the meaning as I read (e.g., "I read a complex paragraph and understood the main idea immediately").
I can comprehend complex text without needing to reread, using fluency and accuracy to support my understanding.
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text with good accuracy and fluency, which helps me understand what I am reading (e.g., "I read a paragraph fluently and understood the main idea").
I can understand most of the text I read the first time without needing to reread.
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read with some accuracy and fluency but may need help understanding parts of the text (e.g., "I read the text aloud but needed help to understand what it meant").
I can reread parts of the text with support to improve my comprehension.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can try to read grade-level text with help, improving my fluency and accuracy with practice (e.g., "With help, I read the sentence more accurately and understood its meaning").
I can understand the text better when someone helps me with the difficult parts.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.b|5.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can choose italics, underlining or quotation marks correctly for any kind of title and explain the rule.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can use italics, underlining or quotation marks correctly to show titles of works.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can put quotation marks around a story title using a model.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can find a title in a sentence with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.b|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.c|5.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: c. spell grade-level words correctly using reference materials to solve words and edit written work as needed.
WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.c|5.ee_text: Spell untaught word phonetically, drawing on letter-sound relationships and common spelling patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced:
I can read grade-level text aloud with great accuracy, appropriate pacing, and strong expression, making the text sound natural and engaging (e.g., "I used different tones for each character’s dialogue and paused correctly at commas").
I can improve my reading each time I practice, making fewer mistakes and adding more expression (e.g., "After practising, I read the speech aloud with the right speed and enthusiasm").
descriptors.cc_at_target:
I can read grade-level text aloud with good accuracy, rate, and expression (e.g., "I read the story at a steady pace and changed my voice to match the mood").
I can improve my accuracy and expression after reading a text a few times (e.g., "When I practised, I used more expression and read with fewer mistakes").
descriptors.cc_approaching:
I can read aloud with some accuracy and expression but may need help adjusting my speed (e.g., "I read the text aloud but needed help slowing down during longer sentences").
I can improve my reading with practice and guidance (e.g., "I read the paragraph better after practising with help to pause at commas").
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can read aloud with help and improve my speed and expression with practice (e.g., "With help, I read the sentence more smoothly and used a happy tone for the characters").
I can read more clearly and expressively after practising multiple times with guidance (e.g., "I practiced reading the story and used better pauses and emotion").
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can spell new words by sounding them out, using what I know about letter sounds and spelling patterns.
I can use what I know about letters and sounds to spell words that I haven’t learned yet.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can try to spell words I don’t know by saying the sounds I hear with help.
I can write some letters that match the sounds of a word with guidance.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can listen to a word and say or write one of the sounds I hear with support.
I can use pictures or letters to show how a word sounds with help.

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.c|5.descriptor_flag: School descriptor may not match this standard

descriptors_suggested.cc_advanced: I can spell grade-level and challenging words correctly and use several reference tools to check and edit my work.
descriptors_suggested.cc_at_target: I can spell grade-level words correctly, using reference materials to solve words and edit my writing.
descriptors_suggested.cc_approaching: I can spell common words correctly and use a dictionary or spell-checker with support.
descriptors_suggested.cc_emerging: I can spell a few familiar words and copy others from a word wall with help.
descriptors_suggested.ee_at_target: I can spell untaught words by sounding them out and using common spelling patterns.

WI-CC-ELA|L.5.6.c|5.source: Awsaj EE ELA New Standards 2025 V1 Complete (school sheet, K-5)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.1|6.text: Cite textual evidence to support an analysis of what the text says explicitly or implicitly and make logical inferences. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.1|6.ee_text: Determine what a text says explicitly as well as what simple inferences should be drawn. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can cite several pieces of strong evidence and explain how each one supports my inference about a text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can cite text evidence to support what a text says directly and the logical inferences I make.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can point to a sentence in the text that supports an answer when my teacher gives me a sentence starter.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can answer simple who, what and where questions using words I find in the text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find what a text says and make a simple inference from it.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.1|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.2|6.text: Summarize texts, from a variety of genres, to determine a theme or central idea and how it is developed by key supporting details over the course of a text. (RI &RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.2|6.ee_text: Determine details in a text that are related to the theme or main idea. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an objective summary and explain how several key details work together to develop the theme or central idea.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize a text and explain how key supporting details develop its theme or central idea.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can retell the main events or facts and name the central idea using a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what a short text is mostly about using pictures or a word bank with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find details in a text that connect to the theme or main idea.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.2|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.3|6.text: In literary texts, describe how events unfold, as well as how characters respond or change as the plot moves toward a resolution. (RL) In informational texts, analyze how individuals, events, and ideas are introduced, related to each other, and developed. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.3|6.ee_text: In literary texts, identify how a character responds to a challenge in a text. (RL) In informational texts, identify a detail that elaborates upon individuals, events, or ideas introduced in a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how a character's changes or an idea's development shape the meaning of the whole text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can describe how a plot unfolds and how characters change, and explain how people, events and ideas are introduced and developed in informational text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put the main events of a story in order and say how a character feels or changes with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the characters and one event in a story or one key person or event in a text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell how a character responds to a problem or find a detail that tells more about a person, event or idea.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.3|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.4|6.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood, including words with multiple meanings within a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.4|6.ee_text: Determine how word choice changes the meaning in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how an author's word choices, including figurative and connotative language, create a specific tone or mood across a text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine the meaning of words, including figurative and connotative meanings, and explain how word choice affects meaning, tone and mood.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use context clues to work out what a word or phrase means and say if it feels positive or negative with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a new word to its meaning using a picture or word bank with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell how a changed word changes the meaning of a sentence or text.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.4|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.5|6.text: In literary texts, analyze how a sentence, paragraph, stanza, chapter, scene, or section fits into the overall structure and how it contributes to the development of theme, central idea, setting, or plot. (RL) In informational texts, analyze how a particular sentence, paragraph, chapter, or section fits into the overall structure of a text and how it contributes to the development of theme or central ideas. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.5|6.ee_text: Given guidance and support determine the structure of a text (e.g., story, poem, drama, argument, directions, informational). (RI &RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how two texts use structure differently and explain how each structure shapes the theme or central idea.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how a sentence, paragraph, chapter, scene or section fits into the structure of a text and helps develop its theme, central idea, setting or plot.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell where a part of the text belongs (beginning, middle or end) and say what it adds with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort texts into story, poem or information text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, tell the structure of a text, such as story, poem, drama, argument, directions or information.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.5|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.6|6.text: In literary texts, identify possible biases, the point of view, and explain how it is developed and conveys meaning in diverse texts. (RL) In informational texts, explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, or culture affect perspective. Analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.6|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, identify words or phrases in the text that describe or show the narrator, speaker, or author’s point of view. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how an author's background and possible bias shape a text and compare it with another author's view of the same topic.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can identify point of view and possible bias in literary texts and explain how an author's location, identity or culture affects perspective in informational texts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell who is telling a story or what the author thinks about a topic using clue words with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a story is told by a character or a narrator with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, find words or phrases that show the narrator's, speaker's or author's point of view.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.6|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.7|6.text: Compare and contrast how different formats, including print and digital media, contribute to the understanding of a subject. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.7|6.ee_text: Find similarities in information presented in different media or formats as well as in text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate which format (print, audio, video or digital) best helps an audience understand a subject and explain why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare and contrast how print and digital formats each help me understand a subject.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list what I learned from a text and from a video on the same subject using a chart with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to the same fact in a text and in a picture or video with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find information that is the same in a text and in another media format.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.7|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.8|6.text: Trace and evaluate the development of an argument and specific claims in texts, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and relevant evidence from claims that are not. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.8|6.ee_text: Distinguish claims in a text supported by reason. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how well an argument is built and explain which claims are strongest and weakest and why.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can trace an argument and its claims, and tell which claims are supported by reasons and evidence and which are not.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find the author's main claim and one reason that supports it using a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what the author wants me to think or do with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell which claims in a text are supported by a reason.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.8|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.9|6.text: Evaluate the quality of texts. Make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, and personal experiences. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.6.9|6.ee_text: Compare and contrast how two texts describe details and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras, or personal experiences. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can develop my own criteria to judge the quality of texts and connect them to other texts, cultures, eras and my own life.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can evaluate the quality of a text and make connections to other texts, ideas, cultural perspectives, identities, eras and my own experiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can say whether I liked a text and give one reason, and connect it to another text or my life with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell how a story is like something in my own life using pictures or sentence starters.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can compare how two texts describe details and connect them to other texts, ideas, cultures or my own experiences.

WI-CC-ELA|R.6.9|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.1|6.text: Compose reflective, formal, and creative writing, which may happen simultaneously or independently, for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.1|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, use drawing, dictating, or writing to compose writing for a variety of high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the best form (reflective, formal or creative) for different purposes and explain my choice.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write reflective, formal and creative pieces for both high-stakes and low-stakes purposes.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a short piece for a given purpose using a model and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can draw, dictate or write a few words to share an idea with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, draw, dictate or write to share my ideas for different purposes.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.1|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.a|6.text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Write arguments to support claims with clear reasons, relevant evidence, and literary theory.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.a|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: a. Write an argument with a clearly stated claim about a topic and include clear reasons to support that claim.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an argument that supports a claim with strong reasons and evidence and responds to an opposing view.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an argument that supports a claim with clear reasons and relevant evidence.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can state my opinion and give one or two reasons using an organizer and sentence frames.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say or write what I think about a topic and why with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate a clear claim about a topic and give clear reasons for it.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.b|6.text: Write text in a variety of modes. b. Write informative texts to examine a topic and convey ideas, concepts, and information through the selection, organization, and analysis of relevant content.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.b|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: b. Write informative texts which introduce a topic and provide facts, details, and/or multimedia content to develop the topic.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an informative text that analyzes a topic in depth, using well-chosen facts, formatting and visuals.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write an informative text that examines a topic and conveys ideas and information by choosing and organizing relevant content.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a short paragraph about a topic with a topic sentence and facts using a frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share facts about a topic using words, pictures or dictation with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate an informative text that introduces a topic and gives facts and details.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.c|6.text: Write text in a variety of modes. c. Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective narrative techniques, relevant descriptive details, and well-structured event sequences.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.c|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: c. Write narratives to convey events and experiences, real or imagined. d. Include dialogue, details regarding what happened, and tell about the events in the order in which they occurred.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a narrative with dialogue, pacing and vivid description that keeps the reader engaged.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write a narrative about real or imagined events using narrative techniques, descriptive details and a clear sequence of events.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a short story with a beginning, middle and end using a story map.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell or draw what happened first, next and last with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate a narrative that tells events in order and includes details.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.2.c|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.a|6.text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Introduce a topic; organize ideas, concepts, and information. Provide a concluding statement appropriate to the mode of writing.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.a|6.ee_text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can organize complex ideas so each part builds on the last and end with a conclusion that adds insight.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can introduce a topic, organize ideas and information, and write a conclusion that fits the mode of writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use a graphic organizer to plan an introduction, body and conclusion.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can put my ideas in order (first, then, last) with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, create a text with an introduction, body and conclusion.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.b|6.text: Create writing that utilizes: b. Transitions: Use appropriate transitions to clarify the relationships among ideas and concepts.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.b|6.ee_text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose varied transitions that clearly show how complex ideas connect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use appropriate transitions to show how ideas and concepts are related.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add transitions such as first, next, because and finally from a word bank.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use simple linking words such as and or then with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, use transitions and time-order words to link my ideas.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.c|6.text: Create writing that utilizes: c. Word Choice (including domain specific): Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to inform about or explain the topic. Use sensory language to describe experiences and events.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.c|6.ee_text: Use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose precise, domain-specific and sensory words to make my writing vivid and exact.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to explain a topic and sensory language to describe experiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can replace general words with more exact words from a word bank with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use labels and simple describing words to tell about a picture or topic.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, use words that give specific details.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.3.c|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.4|6.text: Independently and collaboratively produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.)
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.4|6.ee_text: Produce writing that is appropriate for the task, purpose, or audience.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can adapt the style and organization of my writing for different tasks, purposes and audiences and explain my choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can independently and with others produce clear writing whose development, organization and style fit the task, purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can produce writing that fits a task when I use a model or checklist.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can write or dictate a few sentences on a topic with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can produce writing that fits the task, purpose or audience.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.4|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.5|6.text: With some guidance and support from peers and adults, develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.5|6.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults and peers, plan before writing and produce writing focused on the planned topic, and revise and edit their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently revise my writing using feedback and explain how my changes make it stronger.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can, with some help from peers and adults, plan, revise, edit and rewrite to strengthen my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can make one or two changes to my writing using a revision checklist and teacher feedback.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can fix a capital letter or add a word when an adult points to it.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, plan my writing and revise and edit it.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.5|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.6|6.text: Use technology, (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, or other interactive formats), to produce and publish writing and present the relationships between information and ideas efficiently, as well as, to interact and collaborate with others. Proficiently produce writing through printing, cursive, or typing (with sufficient command of keyboarding skills to type a minimum of three pages in a single sitting), selecting the method(s) best suited for audience and purpose.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.6|6.ee_text: Use digital tools, including the Internet, to produce and publish writing while interacting and collaborating with others. Produce writing through printing, cursive, and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the best technology for my audience and use it to publish and collaborate efficiently.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use technology to produce and publish writing, show how ideas connect and collaborate with others, and type at least three pages in one sitting.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can type and publish a short piece using a template with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a device to type or record a few words with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use digital tools to produce and publish writing and work with others.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.6|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.7|6.text: Conduct short inquiry projects to answer a question, drawing on several sources and refocusing the inquiry when appropriate.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.7|6.ee_text: With guidance and support, conduct short inquiry projects to answer a question.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design my own inquiry question and refocus my research as I learn more from several sources.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct short inquiry projects to answer a question using several sources and refocus when needed.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can answer a research question using two given sources and a note-taking frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find one fact about a topic in a book or website with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, conduct a short inquiry project to answer a question.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.7|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.8|6.text: Gather relevant information from multiple print and digital sources, assess the credibility of each source, quote or paraphrase the data and conclusions of others while avoiding plagiarism and providing basic bibliographic information for sources.
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.8|6.ee_text: Gather information about a given topic from multiple print or digital sources.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can judge the credibility of sources and smoothly blend quotes and paraphrases with full citations.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can gather information from print and digital sources, assess their credibility, quote or paraphrase without plagiarizing, and give basic source information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can take notes from two sources in my own words and list the titles with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can copy a fact and the title of the book or website it came from with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can gather information about a topic from several print or digital sources.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.8|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.9|6.text: Draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and inquiry. (Apply grade 6 Reading standards)
WI-CC-ELA|W.6.9|6.ee_text: With guidance and support from adults, draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support reflection or inquiry questions based on a reading of a literary or informational text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the strongest evidence from texts and explain how it supports my analysis or reflection.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can draw evidence from literary or informational texts to support analysis, reflection and inquiry.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find a quote that supports my answer using a sentence starter.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a picture or sentence that matches my idea with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, use evidence from a text to support my reflection or answer an inquiry question.

WI-CC-ELA|W.6.9|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.a|6.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. a. Come to discussions prepared and explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence on the topic, text, or issue. Support analysis by making connections, paraphrasing, clarifying, or explaining the evidence.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.a|6.ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. a. Come to discussions prepared to share information, with evidence.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can come to discussions with well-chosen evidence and use it to explain and extend my peers' ideas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can come to discussions prepared and refer to evidence, making connections, paraphrasing or explaining to support analysis.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can bring notes to a discussion and share one piece of evidence using a sentence frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share a picture or fact I prepared when asked with support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can come to discussions prepared to share information and evidence.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.b|6.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. b. With guidance and support, set specific norms and goals for collegial discussions (e.g., gaining attention in respectful ways, actively listening, speaking one at a time about the topics and texts under discussion).
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.b|6.ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. b. With guidance and support from adults and peers, follow simple, agreed-upon norms for discussions and contribute information.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can help my group create norms and goals and remind others to follow them respectfully.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can, with guidance, set specific norms and goals for discussions and follow them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can follow class discussion norms such as taking turns when reminded.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can listen and wait for my turn with adult support.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, follow simple discussion norms and contribute information.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.c|6.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. c. Pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail by making comments that contribute to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.c|6.ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. c. Ask and answer questions specific to the topic, text, or issue under discussion.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can ask questions that deepen a discussion and respond with detailed comments that move it forward.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can pose and respond to specific questions with elaboration and detail that add to the discussion.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can ask or answer a question about the topic using question stems.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can answer a yes or no question about the topic with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can ask and answer questions about the topic under discussion.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.c|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.d|6.text: Engage effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing one’s thinking clearly. d. Review the key ideas expressed and demonstrate an understanding of multiple perspectives through reflection and paraphrasing.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.d|6.ee_text: Engage in collaborative discussions. d. Restate key ideas expressed in the discussion

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can summarize the key ideas of a discussion and explain how different perspectives changed my thinking.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can review key ideas and show I understand multiple perspectives by reflecting and paraphrasing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can repeat one key idea from the discussion using a sentence frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to or say a word that shows what the group talked about with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can restate key ideas from a discussion.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.1.d|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.2|6.text: Interpret information presented in diverse media and formats and explain how it contributes to a topic, text, or issue under study.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.2|6.ee_text: Identify information presented in diverse media and formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) that relates to a topic, text, or issue under study.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how information from different media adds to my understanding and judge which source is most useful.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret information from different media and formats and explain how it adds to a topic, text or issue.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell one thing I learned from a chart, video or talk using a frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a picture or chart that shows the topic with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify information in different media and formats that relates to a topic.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.2|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.3|6.text: Understand and evaluate a speaker’s argument and specific claims, distinguishing claims that are supported by reasons and evidence from claims that are not.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.3|6.ee_text: Identify the reasons and evidence supporting the claims made by the speaker.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how convincing a speaker's argument is and explain which claims lack enough evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can understand and evaluate a speaker's argument and tell which claims are supported by reasons and evidence and which are not.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the speaker's claim and one reason using a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what the speaker wants me to think with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the reasons and evidence a speaker uses to support claims.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.3|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.4|6.text: Present claims and findings in a logical order using relevant evidence and details to highlight main ideas or themes. Communicate clearly and in an engaging manner, considering the audience, purpose, and situation. Explain purpose of language choices.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.4|6.ee_text: Clearly present findings on a topic including descriptions, facts, or details, considering the audience.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can present findings in a logical, engaging way, adjust for my audience and explain my language choices.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can present claims and findings in a logical order with evidence and details, speaking clearly for my audience and purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can present a short report using notes or cue cards with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share one fact about a topic with an adult or partner using a picture.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can clearly present findings on a topic with descriptions, facts or details for my audience.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.4|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.5|6.text: Include multimedia components and visual displays in presentations to clarify and enhance information.
WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.5|6.ee_text: Select an auditory, visual, or tactual display to clarify the information in presentations.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can design multimedia and visual displays that make complex information clear and memorable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can include multimedia and visual displays in presentations to clarify and enhance information.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add a picture or chart to my presentation from a choice of options.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can choose a picture that matches my topic with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can select an audio, visual or tactile display to clarify information in my presentation.

WI-CC-ELA|SL.6.5|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.a|6.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. a. Recognize that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history that is implicated in power relationships.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.a|6.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. Notice that standardized English is only one dialect of many and has a specific history.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how the history of standardized English connects to power and compare it with other dialects I know.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize that standardized English is one dialect of many and that its history is connected to power.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one difference between how people speak at home and at school with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can notice that people speak in different ways in different places with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can notice that standardized English is one dialect of many with its own history.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.b|6.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. b. Determine the language demands of a writing or speaking situation, respond in appropriate ways (e.g., precise and concise language, extended and descriptive language, incorporation of code-meshing, etc.).
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.b|6.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. b. Notice the language demands of a writing/speaking situation (i.e. formal, informal) and respond in an appropriate way.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the language demands of different situations and shift my language, including code-meshing, on purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine the language demands of a writing or speaking situation and respond in appropriate ways.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a situation is formal or informal and choose matching words with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort phrases into school talk and friend talk with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can notice whether a situation is formal or informal and respond in an appropriate way.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.c|6.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. c. Expand, combine, and reduce sentences for meaning, reader or listener interest, and style.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.c|6.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. c. Expand or combine sentences for meaning, interest, and style.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can expand, combine and cut sentences on purpose to control rhythm, interest and style.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can expand, combine and reduce sentences for meaning, reader interest and style.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can combine two short sentences using and, but or because with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can add one word to make a sentence longer with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can expand or combine sentences for meaning, interest and style.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.c|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.d|6.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. d. Maintain consistency in style and tone.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.d|6.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. d. Maintain consistency in use of language.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can keep a consistent style and tone across a long piece and explain why it fits my purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can maintain a consistent style and tone in my writing and speaking.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can check a short piece for one change in tone using a checklist with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a sentence sounds friendly or serious with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can keep my use of language consistent.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.1.d|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.a|6.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. a. Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.a|6.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. a. Use context to determine which word is missing from a content area text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can check the meaning of a new word in several ways and explain which strategy helped most.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can verify my first guess about a word's meaning by checking context or a dictionary.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can guess a word's meaning from context and check it in a dictionary with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a new word in a picture dictionary with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use context to work out which word is missing from a text.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.b|6.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. b. Use grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.b|6.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. b. Use frequently occurring root words (e.g., like) and the words that result when affixes are added (e.g., liked, disliked, liking). c. Seek clarification and meaning support when unfamiliar words are encountered while reading or communicating.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use Greek and Latin roots and affixes to work out the meanings of unfamiliar academic words.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to a word's meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find a known root or affix in a word and use a chart to guess its meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a small word I know inside a bigger word with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use root words and affixes to understand words and ask for help with unfamiliar words.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.2.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.a|6.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. a. Determine the denotative, connotative, and figurative meanings of words and phrases used in texts; when words have similar denotations, be able to describe differences in connotation and their impact on meaning and tone.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.a|6.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and use. a. Determine the meaning of words in a text, distinguish between literal and non-literal language.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how connotation shapes tone and choose words with the exact shade of meaning I need.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine denotative, connotative and figurative meanings of words and explain how differences in connotation affect meaning and tone.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a word has a positive or negative feeling using examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a phrase means exactly what it says with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can determine word meanings in a text and tell literal from non-literal language.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.b|6.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. b. Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.b|6.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and use. b. Identify the meaning of simple similes (e.g., The man was as big as a tree.).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can interpret different figures of speech and explain how they add meaning to a text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can interpret figures of speech, such as personification, in context.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain what a simple personification or simile means with a picture or example.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a simile to its meaning with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify the meaning of simple similes.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.c|6.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. c. Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause and effect) to better understand each of the words.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain how word relationships, such as cause and effect or part and whole, deepen meaning in complex texts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use the relationship between words, such as cause and effect, to understand each word better.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort word pairs by relationship (cause and effect) using a chart with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a cause picture to an effect picture with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.c|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.d|6.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. d. Distinguish between words with similar definitions (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.d|6.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and use. d. Demonstrate understanding of words by identifying other words with similar and different meanings

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose the most precise word from a group of synonyms and explain the difference in meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can distinguish between words with similar definitions, such as stingy, economical and thrifty.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can put similar words in order from weakest to strongest with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a word to a word that means almost the same with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify words with similar and different meanings.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.3.d|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.4|6.text: Demonstrate an ability to collaboratively and independently build vocabulary knowledge when encountering unknown words including cultural, general academic, and discipline-specific terms and phrases; make intentional vocabulary choices appropriate to the context and situation.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.4|6.ee_text: Use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases across contexts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently build my vocabulary and choose words that fit different cultural, academic and subject contexts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can build vocabulary with others and on my own, including cultural, academic and subject words, and choose words that fit the situation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use new academic words from a word wall in my speaking and writing with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a few key subject words with pictures and help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use general academic and subject-specific words across contexts.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.4|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.a|6.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: a. use of objective, subjective, possessive, and intensive pronouns; and
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.a|6.ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use personal pronouns (e.g., he, she, they) per the preference of the subject.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use objective, subjective, possessive and intensive pronouns correctly and explain why each fits.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use objective, subjective, possessive and intensive pronouns correctly in writing and speaking and explain my choices.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can choose the correct pronoun (he, him, his) to complete a sentence with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use I, me and my correctly with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use personal pronouns that match the person I am talking about.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.b|6.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: b. strategies to improve expression in conventional language.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.b|6.ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. b. Use indefinite pronouns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use several strategies to improve how I express ideas and explain how they help my reader.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can fix one sentence using a model with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say a complete sentence with an adult model.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use indefinite pronouns such as someone and everything.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.5.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.a|6.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: a. commas, parentheses, and dashes, and
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.a|6.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. a. Use question marks at the end of written questions.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use commas, parentheses and dashes to add information and explain how each changes the effect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use commas, parentheses and dashes correctly in my writing and explain their purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add commas to a list or after an introductory word with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the commas in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use question marks at the end of written questions.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.a|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.b|6.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: b. correct spelling.
WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.b|6.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. b. Spell untaught words phonetically, drawing on letter-sound relationships and common spelling patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can spell grade-level words correctly and use spelling patterns and resources to spell complex words.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can spell correctly in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can spell common words correctly and use a word wall or spell-checker for others.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can spell my name and a few familiar words with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can spell new words by sounding them out and using common spelling patterns.

WI-CC-ELA|L.6.6.b|6.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.1|7.text: Cite textual evidence to support an analysis of what the text says explicitly or implicitly and make logical inferences. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.1|7.ee_text: Analyze text to identify where information is explicitly stated and where inferences must be drawn. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can cite the strongest evidence for my inferences and explain why some evidence is stronger than other evidence.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can cite several pieces of text evidence to support my analysis of what the text says directly and the inferences I make.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find one or two sentences that support my answer using a sentence starter.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a word or sentence in the text that answers a simple question with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify where information is stated directly in a text and where I must make an inference.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.1|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.2|7.text: Summarize texts, from a variety of genres, to determine a theme or central idea and analyze its development over the course of the text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.2|7.ee_text: Determine details in a text that are related to the theme or main idea and how it is developed over the course of a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write an objective summary and analyze how two or more central ideas or themes develop and interact across a text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can summarize a text and analyze how its theme or central idea develops over the course of the text.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the central idea and list key details in order using a graphic organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what a short text is mostly about using a picture or word bank with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find details related to the theme or main idea and tell how it develops across the text.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.2|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.3|7.text: In literary texts, analyze how elements of plot are related, affect one another, and contribute to meaning. (RL) In informational texts, analyze how individuals, events, and ideas are introduced, related to each other, and developed. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.3|7.ee_text: In literary texts determine how two or more story elements are related. (RL) In informational texts, identify how two individuals, events, or ideas are related. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how plot elements or people, events and ideas influence one another to shape the meaning of a text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how plot elements affect each other and contribute to meaning, and how people, events and ideas are introduced and developed in informational texts.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain how one event causes another in a story or text using a cause and effect chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can name the setting, a character and an event with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell how two story elements, or two people, events or ideas, are related.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.3|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.4|7.text: Determine the meaning of words and phrases, including figurative and connotative meanings. Analyze the impact of specific word choices on meaning, tone, and mood, including words with multiple meanings within a text. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.4|7.ee_text: Determine how word choice changes the meaning in a text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how repeated word choices and figurative language build tone and mood across a whole text.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine the meaning of words, including figurative and connotative meanings, and analyze how word choice affects meaning, tone and mood.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use context clues to define a word and tell whether it sounds positive or negative with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a new word with its meaning using a picture or word bank with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can tell how word choice changes the meaning in a text.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.4|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.5|7.text: In literary texts, analyze how structure, including genre-specific features, contributes to the development of themes or central ideas. (RL) In informational texts, analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how the sections contribute to the whole and to the development of themes or central ideas. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.5|7.ee_text: Given guidance and support, compare the structure of two or more texts (e.g., stories, poems, dramas, argument, directions, informational) and determine how a fact, step, or event fits into the overall structure of the text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can compare how different genres or text structures develop the same theme or central idea.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how a text's structure, including genre features and sections, contributes to the development of themes or central ideas.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name the structure of a text (such as sequence or problem and solution) using a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what comes first, next and last in a text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, compare the structure of two texts and tell how a fact, step or event fits into the structure.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.5|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.6|7.text: In literary texts, analyze how an author develops and contrasts the point of view, possible biases, and the perspectives of different characters or narrators. (RL) In informational texts, explain how an author’s geographic location, identity, or culture affect perspective. Analyze how the author distinguishes his or her position from that of others. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.6|7.ee_text: Identify words or phrases in the text that describe or show the narrator, speaker, or author’s point of view. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how authors contrast perspectives and biases and how a writer's culture or location shapes their position compared with others.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can analyze how an author develops and contrasts points of view, biases and perspectives, and explain how an author's background shapes perspective.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell the point of view of two characters or the author using clue words with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell who is telling a story with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can find words or phrases that show the narrator's, speaker's or author's point of view.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.6|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.7|7.text: Compare and contrast a written text with audio, filmed, staged, or digital versions in order to analyze the effects of techniques unique to each media and each format’s portrayal of a subject. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.7|7.ee_text: Compare a text to an audio, video, or multimedia version of the same text. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate how techniques in audio, film, stage or digital versions change the meaning of a text compared with the written version.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can compare a written text with audio, filmed, staged or digital versions and analyze the effects of each format's techniques.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can list what is the same and different between a text and its video version using a Venn diagram.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a scene in a video that matches part of the text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can compare a text with an audio, video or multimedia version of the same text.

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.7|7.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|R.7.8|7.text: Trace and evaluate the development of an argument and specific claims in a text. Assess whether the reasoning is valid and the evidence is relevant and sufficient. Recognize when irrelevant evidence is introduced. (RI)
WI-CC-ELA|R.7.8|7.ee_text: Determine how a claim or reason fits into the overall structure of a text. (RI)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can evaluate an argument and explain how irrelevant or weak evidence affects its overall strength.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can trace and evaluate an argument, judging whether reasoning is valid and evidence is relevant and sufficient, and notice irrelevant evidence.
