WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.b|8.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. b. Determine the language demands of a writing or speaking situation; respond in appropriate ways (e.g., precise and concise language, extended and descriptive language, incorporation of code-meshing, etc.).
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.b|8.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. b. Notice the language demands of a writing/speaking situation (i.e. formal, informal) and respond in an appropriate way.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze the language demands of complex situations and shift my language, including code-meshing, on purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine the language demands of a writing or speaking situation and respond in appropriate ways.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell if a situation is formal or informal and choose matching words with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can sort phrases into school talk and friend talk with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can notice whether a situation is formal or informal and respond in an appropriate way.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.b|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.c|8.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. c. Use verbs in the active and passive voice and in the conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects (e.g., emphasizing the actor or the action, expressing uncertainty, or describing a state contrary to fact).
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.c|8.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. c. Use to-be verbs (am, are, is, was, were, be, become, became) accurately when writing and communicating.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose active or passive voice and conditional or subjunctive mood on purpose and explain the effect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use verbs in active and passive voice and in conditional and subjunctive mood to achieve particular effects.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can change a sentence from passive to active voice using a model.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use is, are and was correctly in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use to-be verbs (am, are, is, was, were) correctly when writing and communicating.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.c|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.d|8.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. d. Begin to develop metacognitive awareness as writers and speakers by explaining the reasons for language choices.
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.d|8.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. d. Begin to develop metacognitive awareness as writers and speakers by explaining the reasons for language choices.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can explain and evaluate my language choices in detail and revise them to better fit my purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can begin to develop awareness of my language choices by explaining my reasons for them.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain one word choice I made using a sentence frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a word I chose and say why with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can begin to explain the reasons for my language choices.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.1.d|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.a|8.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. a. Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.a|8.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. a. Use context to determine which word is missing from a content area text.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can check a word's meaning with several strategies and explain which one was most reliable.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can verify my first guess about a word's meaning by checking context or a dictionary.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can guess a word's meaning from context and check it in a dictionary with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a new word in a picture dictionary with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use context to work out which word is missing from a text.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.a|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.b|8.text: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words or phrases in grade-level reading and content; use context clues, analyze meaningful word parts, consult general and specialized reference materials, and apply word solving strategies (for meaning) as appropriate. b. Use grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word.
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.b|8.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. b. Use frequently occurring root words (e.g., like) and the words that result when affixes are added (e.g., liked, disliked, liking). c. Seek clarification and meaning support when unfamiliar words are encountered while reading or communicating.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use Greek and Latin roots and affixes to work out and explain the meanings of complex academic words.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to a word's meaning.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find a known root or affix in a word and use a chart to guess its meaning.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find a small word I know inside a bigger word with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use root words and affixes to understand words and ask for help with unfamiliar words.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.2.b|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.3|8.text: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings. Determine the denotative, connotative, and figurative meanings of words and phrases used in texts; when words have similar denotations, be able to describe differences in connotation and their impact on meaning and tone. Analyze the impact of specific word choice on meaning and tone, including analogies or allusions to other texts.
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.3|8.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of word relationships and use. a. Identify the literal and nonliteral meanings of words in context. b. Use descriptive words to add meaning when writing and communicating.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can analyze how connotation, analogies and allusions work together to create meaning and tone.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can determine denotative, connotative and figurative meanings, describe connotation differences, and analyze how word choice, analogies and allusions affect meaning and tone.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can explain a simple analogy and tell whether a word feels positive or negative with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a phrase means exactly what it says with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify literal and nonliteral meanings of words and use descriptive words to add meaning.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.3|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.4|8.text: Demonstrate an ability to collaboratively and independently build vocabulary knowledge when encountering unknown words including cultural, general academic, and discipline-specific terms and phrases; make intentional vocabulary choices appropriate to the context and situation.
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.4|8.ee_text: Use general academic and domain-specific words and phrases across contexts.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently build vocabulary and make intentional word choices for cultural, academic and subject contexts.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can build vocabulary with others and on my own, including cultural, academic and subject terms, and choose words that fit the situation.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use new academic words from a word wall in my speaking and writing with support.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can use a few key subject words with pictures and help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use general academic and subject-specific words across contexts.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.4|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.a|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: a. active and passive voice verbs;
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.a|8.ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. a. Use appropriate verbs to match nouns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can choose active or passive voice to control emphasis and explain why it fits my purpose.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use active and passive voice verbs correctly and explain their purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell whether a sentence is active or passive using examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say who is doing the action in a picture sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use verbs that match their nouns.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.a|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.b|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: b. indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional, and subjunctive mood verbs; and
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.b|8.ee_text: Demonstrate standardized English grammar and usage when communicating. b. Form and use the simple verb tenses (e.g., I walked, I walk, I will walk).

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use all five verb moods on purpose and explain how each changes meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use indicative, imperative, interrogative, conditional and subjunctive mood verbs correctly and explain their purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can sort sentences into statements, commands and questions using a chart.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell a statement from a question with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can form and use simple verb tenses (I walked, I walk, I will walk).

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.b|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.c|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English grammar and usage when writing or speaking. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose of language choice with: c. recognizing and correcting shifts in verb voice and mood.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can find and fix shifts in verb voice and mood in my own and others' writing and explain the confusion they cause.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in verb voice and mood.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can fix a verb shift in a given sentence using a model.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell which of two sentences sounds right with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.5.c|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.a|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: a. punctuation to recognize a pause or break,
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.a|8.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. a. Use end punctuation and capitalization when writing a sentence or question.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use commas, ellipses or dashes to show a pause or break on purpose and explain the effect.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use punctuation to show a pause or break and explain its purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can add punctuation to show a pause in a sentence using examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find the punctuation marks in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use end punctuation and capitals when writing a sentence or question.

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.a|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.b|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: b. ellipsis to indicate an omission, and

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can use ellipses to show omissions in quotations and explain how they keep the original meaning.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can use an ellipsis to show an omission and explain its purpose.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use an ellipsis to shorten a quote using a model.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find an ellipsis in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: Not applicable

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.b|8.source: Wisconsin Standards for ELA (DPI 2020); Wisconsin Essential Elements for ELA (DPI 2022)

WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.c|8.text: Demonstrate contextually appropriate use of the conventions of standardized English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing. Discern when and where it is appropriate to use standardized English. Appropriately use and explain the intended purpose in conventions with: c. correct spelling.
WI-CC-ELA|L.8.6.c|8.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. c. Spell words phonetically, drawing on knowledge of letter-sound relationships and/or common spelling patterns.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can spell grade-level and complex words correctly and use patterns and resources to check my spelling.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can spell correctly in my writing.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can spell common words correctly and use a word wall or spell-checker for others.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can spell my name and a few familiar words with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can spell words by using letter-sound relationships and common spelling patterns.

WI-CC-ELA|R.9-10.1|9.text: Cite relevant textual evidence that strongly supports analysis of what the text says explicitly or implicitly and make logical inferences; develop questions for further exploration. (RI&RL)
WI-CC-ELA|R.9-10.1|9.ee_text: Determine which citations demonstrate what the text says explicitly as well as inferentially. (RI&RL)

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can cite highly relevant textual evidence to support deep analysis of explicit and implicit content and develop insightful questions for deeper understanding and further exploration.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can cite relevant textual evidence that strongly supports an analysis of what the text says explicitly or implicitly and make logical inferences; icluding develop questions for further exploration.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can find and cite evidence to support my understanding of explicit content in the text.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can determine the meaning of a text and cite textual evidence to draw inferences from the text.
I can use a graphic organizer such as a two-column chart with the headings, “What I Know” and “Facts”. Fill in the graphic organizer by using examples from text of “Facts” (e.g., “Steps are numbered, if I do #3 before I do #2, I don’t have the pieces I need.”) that support an inference “What I Know” (e.g., need to do steps in order).
I can While reading a historical text, infer what will happen next in the text using textual evidence to support the inference (e.g., The soldiers gathered on the battlefield supports an inference that there is going to be a fight).
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can determine which citations demonstrate what the text says explicitly as well as inferentially.
I can draw an inference about an informational text (e.g., It is important to know the weather to plan activities for the day.) and select two facts from a weather report that support the inference (e.g., The weather will be sunny in the morning but it will rain in the afternoon.).
I can after reading a narrative on a march with Martin Luther King, select an inference from choices (e.g., The marchers did not want anyone to get hurt.) and choose a related fact stated in the text to support the inference (e.g., The people did not bring guns or clubs.).
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can determine which citations demonstrate what the text says explicitly.
I can underline text that tells how a task should be completed.
I can given a statement of what the text says explicitly, find the citation in a teacher-selected portion of the text.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can identify words from a text.
I can after shared reading of a familiar informational text, respond by nodding or using a switch to identify a statement read aloud as from a familiar informational text.

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.3.a|10.text: Create writing that utilizes: a. Organization: Introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, analysis, information, and claims to make important connections and distinctions. Establish and maintain a structure and conventions consistent with the mode of writing. Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the topic, themes, and experiences presented in the text.
WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.3.a|10.ee_text: use a combination of drawing, dictating and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can create writing with a suspenseful and engaging introduction, a well-structured body that supports the purpose and topic, and a strong concluding statement that ties up all loose ends.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can introduce a topic; organize complex ideas, concepts, analysis, information, and claims to make important connections and distinctions. Establish and maintain a structure and conventions consistent with the mode of writing. Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the topic, themes, and experiences presented in the text.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can put my ideas in order using a beginning, middle and end organizer with support.

I can use a combination of drawing, dictating, and writing to create a text that includes an introduction, body, and conclusion, uses words that convey specific details, transitions to link and build connections, and temporal words to signal event order.

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.4|9.text: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience. (Grade-specific expectations for writing types are defined in standards 1-3 above.
WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.4|9.ee_text: Produce writing that is appropriate for the task, purpose, and audience.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently and collaboratively produce writing that is clear, coherent, culturally-sustaining, and rhetorically authentic, tailored to the task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are culturally-sustaining and rhetorically authentic to task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can produce writing with clarity and coherence, with attention to task, purpose, and audience.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can produce writing that is complete and appropriate to a particular task, purpose, and audience.
I can write directions in sequence to do a particular task.
I can make a list of things to assemble that will be needed for a class project.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can produce writing that is appropriate to a particular task, purpose, or audience.
I can make a list of things to pack for a trip using a talking word processor with word prediction software.
I can make a list of three or four steps needed to complete a task by responding to questions in graphic organizer software (e.g., List all the things you did. What did you do first? What did you do next? What was the last thing you did?), which is then converted to text outline and imported into talking word processor, where students expands on the notes and checks accuracy.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, produce writing that is appropriate to the task, purpose, or audience.
I can use a word/picture bank projected on an interactive whiteboard combined with spelling to make a list of things to pack for a trip.
I can use a set of guidelines, word prediction software, and a talking word processor to write a letter with of application with an introduction, body, and a closing.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, write.
I can use a keyboard to type letters interactively with a peer who provides a model by writing conventionally but simply.
I can use a multiple message voice output device interfaced with a computer and help from an adult who navigates to the desired page to make a list of free choice activities and then types letter-by-letter about each activity.

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.4|10.source: Awsaj G9-10 ELA New Standards 2024 (school sheet)

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.5|9.text: Develop and strengthen writing (collaboratively and individually) as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.5|9.ee_text: with guidance and support from adults and peers as needed, plan before writing, produce writing for a specific purpose and focused on a planned topic, and revise and edit their own writing, dictation, or pictures.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently revise and edit my writing, incorporating feedback to enhance clarity and coherence, with a strong focus on purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can develop and strengthen my writing (collaboratively and individually) as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can revise and edit my writing with guidance to improve clarity and address purpose and audience.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can strengthen writing by planning and revising own writing and adding more information.
I can given a topic and a sample brainstorming bubble, generate ideas and write them down, then reread what is written and add one more detail.
I can Develop outline before beginning the writing process (topic, three details, conclusion) and use it to write, seek peer feedback, and then add to the outline based on feedback provided.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can develop writing by planning and revising own writing by adding more information.
I can given a topic and a sample brainstorming bubble, generate ideas and write them down, then reread what is written and add one more detail.
I can Using a question framework (e.g., 5 W’s and an H) in graphic organizer software, take turns entering information into the organizer, seek another peer partner group’s feedback, and then add to the outline.
I can after reading a science text, work with a classmate to take notes in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic representation into an outline, and use word prediction software with a specific topic dictionary to complete the L column of a KWL chart, share it with another pair of classmates, and revise based on their feedback.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, develop writing by planning and revising own writing by adding more information.
I can after sharing writing with peers, work with peers to brainstorm ideas to add. Peers write all of the ideas in a list and give it to the student to use in revising and adding more information to improve the overall quality of the writing.
I can Work with peers to plan a written report of their research project. Each takes turns reading what they have to one another and then the group works together to add ideas to a graphic organizer provided by the teacher. Finally, the student adds ideas from the graphic organizer to own writing to strengthen it.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support from adults and peers, add more to writing to clarify message.
I can When asked by an adult or peer to add more, select additional letters or words to add to the overall message.
I can with teacher guidance and support and using word prediction software (e.g., The teacher asks, “What sound do you hear at the beginning of cat?”), and a talking word processor (e.g., The teacher says, “It said car. I thought you were trying to write cat. What can we change to make it say cat?”), label familiar pictures from a favorite text.

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.6|9.text: make informed and intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, or other interactive formats) to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks for specific purposes and audiences. Such decisions include assessing particular technologies’ affordances for: a. connecting writers and readers, b. producing accessible experiences for specific audiences, and c. dynamically and flexibly matching modes with ideas to communicate with readers.
WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.6|9.ee_text: make intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, and/or other interactive formats) to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products. Proficiently produce writing through printing, cursive, and/or typing.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can make informed and intentional decisions about technology use to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks, assessing particular technologies’ affordances for connecting writers and readers, producing accessible experiences, and dynamically matching modes with ideas.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can make informed and intentional decisions about technology use (including paper and pencil, internet, audio, visual, multilingual, multimodal, mobile, or other interactive formats) to engage in authentic rhetorical tasks for specific purposes and audiences.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can use technology to produce and share my writing, with basic linking and citation of sources.
descriptors.cc_emerging:
I can use technology, including the Internet,to produce, publish, and update individual writing products.
I can use technology to update, edit, and revise a piece of own writing.
I can use a talking word processor to listen to first draft and decide what information to add, spell check and grammar check to edit, and then export digital draft to class wiki.
I can Having published a draft in a digital writing environment (e.g., website, wiki, blog), review comments of classmates about the draft, download it to a talking word processor with word prediction software, revise it based on the feedback, and upload back to the digital writing environment.
descriptors.ee_at_target:
I can use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products.
I can use technology to add a sentence in an electronic shared writing product.
I can add words to sentences in an electronic shared writing product.
I can use online communication software to text message with an e-buddy in another classroom or school.
I can record daily activities on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a traditional home-school notebook.
I can navigate the Internet using screen reader software, identify information about the selected topic, use the information to write using a talking word processor with an alternative keyboard, and share what was learned with classmates.
I can use a teacher-created or teacher-identified website to learn about a topic with a peer, take notes with the peer in graphic organizer software, convert the graphic organizer to an outline, and co-author a summary.
descriptors.ee_approaching:
I can with guidance and support, use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update shared writing products.
I can after reviewing and discussing a shared writing product, add words to sentences in the electronic shared writing product.
I can having sent an e-mail to an adult, read their response seeking additional information or clarification, and write a new e-mail to address the request.
I can use an alternative keyboard programmed with the day’s activities and some comments to write an entry on a blog that is shared with parents instead of a home-school notebook.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance and support, use technology to write.
I can use a keyboard to type letters and words interactively with a peer or an adult who types simple, conventionally spelled messages.
I can use a keyboard programmed for only alphabet letters and a space bar, word prediction software, and a talking word processor with a peer model to take turns typing text messages to one another.

WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.7|9.text: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem that is rhetorically authentic and culturally- sustaining; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating an understanding of the subject under investigation.
WI-CC-ELA|W.9-10.7|9.ee_text: with guidance and support as needed, conduct inquiry projects to answer a question or solve a problem.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can conduct detailed and sustained research projects to answer complex questions, synthesizing multiple sources and generating nuanced related questions for further exploration.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem that is rhetorically authentic and culturally-sustaining; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating an understanding of the subject under investigation.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can conduct inquiry projects to answer questions or solve problems with minimal support.

I can conduct inquiry projects to answer a question or solve a problem with guidance and support as needed.

I can conduct simple inquiry projects with guidance to answer questions or solve problems.
I can with help, research a basic question or problem and share what I learned.
descriptors.ee_emerging:
I can with guidance, participate in simple inquiry activities to answer questions or solve problems.
I can with support, explore a simple question or problem and communicate my findings.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell what happens at the beginning and end of a text with help.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can dictate or write a few words to share an idea with support.

WI-CC-ELA|W.11-12.2.a|11.text: Write text in a variety of modes. a. Write arguments and literary analysis to support claims in an analysis of substantive topics or texts. Establish the significance of the claim(s) using valid reasoning, literary theory, and relevant and sufficient evidence that introduce precise claim(s); distinguish the claim(s) from alternate or opposing claims; and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence. Develop claim(s) and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out the strengths and limitations of both in a manner that anticipates the audience's knowledge level and concerns.
WI-CC-ELA|W.11-12.2.a|11.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: a. Write an argument or literary analysis with a clearly stated claim and valid and sufficient reasons to support the claim. Organize reasons logically and develop the claim fairly.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can write a sophisticated argument or literary analysis that weighs claims and counterclaims fairly and anticipates my audience's concerns.
descriptors.cc_at_target: I can write arguments that introduce precise claims, distinguish counterclaims, and develop both fairly with evidence, organized to show clear relationships.
descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write a claim, a counterclaim and evidence for each using an argument organizer.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can say or write my opinion and one reason with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can, with support, write or dictate an argument with a clear claim and valid reasons organized logically.

WI-CC-ELA|W.11-12.2.b|11.text: Write text in a variety of modes. b. Write informative texts that examine and convey complex ideas, concepts, and information clearly and accurately through the effective selection, organization, and analysis of content by introducing a topic; organizing complex ideas, concepts, and information to make important connections and distinctions; including formatting (e.g., headings), graphics (e.g., figures, tables), and multimedia when useful to aiding comprehension; thoroughly developing the topic by selecting the most significant and relevant well-chosen facts, extended definitions, concrete details, quotations, and other information and examples appropriate to the audience's knowledge of the topic.
WI-CC-ELA|W.11-12.2.b|11.ee_text: With guidance and support, use writing and/or dictation to write in a variety of modes: b. descriptors.cc_approaching: I can write an informative text with headings, facts and quotes using a planning frame.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can share facts about a topic using words, pictures or dictation with help.

WI-CC-ELA|L.11-12.1.e|11.text: Demonstrate an understanding of how language functions in different cultures, contexts, and disciplines; apply this knowledge to comprehend more fully when reading and listening, and make effective choices when composing, creating, and speaking. e. Apply an understanding of syntax to the study of complex texts when reading; vary syntax for effect when writing.
WI-CC-ELA|L.11-12.1.e|11.ee_text: Use language to achieve desired outcomes when communicating. a. WI-CC-ELA|L.11-12.2.b|11.ee_text: Demonstrate knowledge of word meanings. b. Identify and use root words and the words that result when affixes are added or removed. c. descriptors.cc_advanced: I can predict and explain how word changes shift meaning and part of speech across academic vocabulary.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can match a word to a picture of its meaning with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can identify root words and the words formed by adding or removing affixes, and use references to clarify meanings.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can tell the difference in feeling between two similar words using a word scale.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can tell whether a phrase means exactly what it says with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can interpret common figures of speech.

descriptors.cc_advanced: I can independently build vocabulary in several disciplines and choose words precisely for each context.

descriptors.cc_approaching: I can name one convention of a genre, such as a letter or report, using examples.
descriptors.cc_emerging: I can point to a title or heading in a text with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use conventions of standard English when needed.

WI-CC-ELA|L.11-12.6.a|11.ee_text: Demonstrate understanding of conventions of standardized English. a. Demonstrate conventions of standard English including capitalization, ending punctuation, and spelling when writing.

descriptors.cc_emerging: I can find capital letters and end marks in a sentence with help.
descriptors.ee_at_target: I can use capitals, end punctuation and spelling conventions when writing.
